Aggregates the outcome of a routing table lookup: whether a catch-all matched, the matched rule index and blueprint index path, the captured routing parameters, and the HTTP method. Provides default and convenience constructors.

Exception type in the crow namespace representing an HTTP 400 Bad Request error. It derives from std::runtime_error and can be constructed with either a std::string or a C-string message. Debug-only static counter tracking live Connection instances. Present only when CROW_ENABLE_DEBUG is defined.

HTTP request object used by Crow. Holds method, URL, query params, headers, body, client IP, HTTP version, connection flags, and pointers to middleware context/container and the associated asio::io_context. Provides helpers to read headers, check version, parse x-www-form-urlencoded bodies, and schedule handlers on the io_context. Ownership: typically created and managed by the Crow server/router; this header does not define construction beyond its constructors. Destruction is trivial (no custom resources). Ensure io_context is valid before calling post/dispatch.

crow::response represents an HTTP response object in Crow. It holds status code, body, and headers, supports streaming writes, redirect helpers, completion signaling, and serving static files via embedded static_file_info. Instances are typically created and returned by handlers; sending is finalized by end(). Compression control and content-length handling are supported. Move-only assignable; copy assignment deleted.
Nested helper type storing metadata for a static file response: the file path, stat buffer, and stat() return code. Used internally by crow::response to serve files.

Lightweight non-owning (optionally owning) string view used by the JSON reader. Stores begin/end pointers into parsed buffers and supports comparisons. When marked as owned_ it deletes its buffer on destruction. Primarily used for keys and returning string values from rvalue.

Read-only JSON value produced by the crow::json parser. Holds raw pointers into an internal buffer and lazily exposes typed accessors (numbers, booleans, strings, arrays, objects). For arrays/objects it maintains a dynamically grown array of child rvalue nodes and an optional key for object members. Errors are tracked via an internal bit. String nodes may require unescape() before consumption; s() returns a detail::r_string view into the buffer.

Writable/owning JSON value used to assemble and serialize JSON. Stores numbers, strings, arrays, objects, or functions. Provides many constructors and assignment operators for native C++ types, and can be constructed from an rvalue (parsed read value). Inherits returnable to emit application/json bodies via dump().
Helper to read internal data from a wvalue without changing its type. Provides typed get() methods with fallbacks and holds a const reference to a wvalue.

objects.description: Strongly-typed enumeration of logging severity levels used by the crow logging system. Provides standard levels (Debug, Info, Warning, Error, Critical). Uppercase entries are conditionally defined to avoid macro conflicts; canonical values are the capitalized names shown at the end. Used to select filtering and formatting of log messages.
Abstract interface for log handlers. Implementations must provide log(message, level) to consume formatted messages at a given LogLevel. The destructor is virtual to allow polymorphic deletion.
Concrete ILogHandler that writes formatted log messages to std::cerr, including a UTC or local timestamp (depending on CROW_USE_LOCALTIMEZONE) and a fixed-width level tag.

RAII streaming logger. Constructs with a LogLevel, accumulates stream output via operator<< into an internal ostringstream, and on destruction (if CROW_ENABLE_LOGGING and level >= current level) forwards the message to the current ILogHandler. Provides static controls to set/get global log level and handler.
Marker base struct for local (non-global) Crow middleware. It defines a nested typedef `call_global` as `std::false_type` to signal selection logic that the middleware is local-only.
Call-criteria functor that enables only global middleware when iterating the middleware chain. Its `enabled<MW>(index)` returns true iff MW is global.
Forward-iteration specialization that enables middleware whose indices match a provided increasing list. Maintains a mutable slider cursor.
Reverse-iteration specialization that enables middleware whose indices match a provided decreasing list. Uses a mutable slider that moves backward.

Explicit specialization of partial_context for zero middlewares. Serves as the base terminator of the partial_context inheritance chain and defines a partial alias template that resolves to itself for any N.
Represents a single multipart header entry (e.g., Content-Type or Content-Disposition) with its main value and key/value parameters. Provides numeric conversion operators from the value string.

One section of a multipart message. Carries optional headers (as a multimap from name to header object) and the raw body for that section. Provides numeric conversions from the body string and a helper to retrieve a header by name.

A parsed multipart/form-data message. Inherits returnable to support response serialization. Stores headers, boundary, the list of parts, and a name-indexed multimap of parts. Provides constructors from explicit components or directly from a crow::request, parsing the body according to the boundary. Includes dump helpers for serialization of parts.

Small helper for streaming a string_view surrounded by a padding character (default double quote). Intended for pretty-printing header parameter values.

A non-owning view of a single multipart section. Holds header map and body as string_view. Provides implicit numeric conversions by parsing the body, header lookup helper, and a stream formatter that outputs headers and body.

Exception thrown for mustache template compilation or parsing errors. Inherits from std::exception and stores a prefixed error message returned by what().
Returnable HTTP body wrapper produced by template_t::render() or render_string(). Sets content type to text/html and returns the rendered body via dump().
Enumeration of parser actions used during mustache template parsing: regular/escaped tags, block delimiters, else-sections, partials, and ignored items.
Parser action node produced by template_t::parse(). Stores tag character, span indices into the template source, action type, block matching metadata, and jump position for blocks/partials.

Compiled Mustache template. Parses the template source into actions/fragments and renders to string or to a rendered_template with a JSON-like context (crow::mustache::context = crow::json::wvalue). Owns parsing state and provides render APIs.

Represents the query component of a URL parsed into key/value pairs. Stores the original query string buffer and an array of pointers into that buffer for each k/v segment. Provides APIs to get/pop single values, lists, and bracketed dictionaries, plus enumerate keys. Internally relies on qs_parse/qs_k2v/qs_dict_name2kv helpers defined above. Copy/move operations adjust internal pointers to the owning string buffer. The class does not allocate per key/value; values are null-terminated in-place within url_.

Abstract base struct in namespace crow representing a returnable payload from a handler. It stores a content_type string and requires derived classes to implement dump() to serialize to a string. It has a constructor taking the content type and a virtual destructor, enabling safe polymorphic deletion. No further ownership or construction helpers are provided in this header.

Typesafe container of middleware indices for an App’s middleware tuple. Provides accumulation, merge, pack (sort/unique), and access used by Router to decide which middlewares to run for a rule/blueprint.
Abstract base for all route rules. Stores URL pattern, methods bitmask, name, middleware indices, and provides virtual handlers for requests and upgrades. Router owns and invokes derived rules.
Configurable catch‑all handler used when no route matches or method not allowed. Accepts various handler signatures and stores a normalized callable.
Runtime-typed rule where handler signature is erased and verified against URL params. Handles setting mustache base and invokes wrapped handler.
URL routing trie storing per-method route patterns. Supports parameters, blueprint indices, optimization, debug printing, and lookup returning routing_handle_result.
Internal node of Trie representing either a fixed string fragment or a typed parameter, and optionally holding a rule index and blueprint index.
Blueprint groups rules under a common URL prefix and directories. Supports nesting, local middlewares, per-blueprint catchall, and rule creation. Router consumes blueprints to register routes.
direct_api_constructors: crow::Blueprint::Blueprint(const std::string&, const std::string&, const std::string&)

objects.description: Central router mapping methods to Tries and rules. Registers rules and blueprints, validates, performs lookup, dispatches handlers and middlewares, manages upgrades and catchall routing.

Adaptor wrapping a plain TCP socket (asio::ip::tcp::socket). Provides a common interface used by crow for socket operations without SSL. Construction requires an asio::io_context and ignores the context pointer. start(F) immediately invokes the callback with a success error_code.
Adaptor wrapping a Unix domain socket (asio::local::stream_protocol::socket). Provides the same interface as SocketAdaptor but for local stream sockets. start(F) immediately calls back with success.

A scheduler class that runs void() tasks after a configurable number of ticks. Each tick is tick_length_ms_ (default 1 second). Users can schedule tasks with an optional timeout in ticks, cancel tasks by identifier, and adjust a default timeout. Internally uses asio::basic_waitable_timer with steady_clock and periodically processes due tasks. Destructor cancels the timer. Thread-safety details are not specified; intended to be used within the same asio::io_context.
Lightweight exception-like type used by const_str to indicate an out-of-range access during compile-time evaluation. It has a dummy constructor and carries no state.
A constexpr-friendly immutable string wrapper for string literals, providing size, iteration, index access with compile-time bounds checking, and implicit conversion to const char*.
Header defines a namespaced constant character array crow::VERSION holding the library version string "master". No structs, enums, classes, or typedefs are defined in this file.
Finite-state machine states used by the websocket frame reader inside crow::websocket::Connection. Guides parsing of the incoming WebSocket frames (header, extended length, mask, and payload).

objects.description: WebSocket close status codes as defined by RFC 6455 section 7.4.1, plus ranges for library/private use. Used when closing connections and reporting reasons.

Abstract base class representing a WebSocket connection. Defines the interface for sending frames (text/binary/ping/pong), closing, querying remote IP and negotiated subprotocol, and storing user data pointer.

Middleware struct that parses incoming Cookie headers into a key/value jar and allows handlers to queue Set-Cookie headers for the response. Provides before_handle to parse cookies and after_handle to emit Set-Cookie for any queued cookies in context.

Represents a single HTTP cookie with attributes (Domain, Path, Secure, HttpOnly, Expires, Max-Age, SameSite). Provides fluent setters and a dump() method to format into a Set-Cookie header value. Copyable; internally uses owning unique_ptrs for optional attributes.
Enum class for the Cookie SameSite attribute values: Strict, Lax, or None.

Per-request middleware context storing parsed incoming cookies in jar and a queue of outgoing cookies_to_add. Provides getters and setters for cookies; owned and accessed by CookieParser during request/response lifecycle.

Fluent rule-set builder for configuring Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) headers. It accumulates policy values (origin, methods, headers, exposed headers, max-age, credentials) and applies them to a response. Instances are created and owned by CORSHandler (global or per-prefix/blueprint). Construction is restricted: no public constructor; only CORSHandler creates instances. Methods are chainable. Call ignore() to disable CORS header emission for the associated scope.

Crow middleware that manages and applies CORS policies. Holds a global default CORSRules and optional per-prefix/per-blueprint rules. On after_handle, selects the matching rules by URL prefix and applies headers to the response. Provides factory methods to obtain and modify rules for a prefix, blueprint, or global scope.

objects.description: Empty middleware context structure for CORSHandler to satisfy Crow middleware interface. It carries no state.
Type-safe variant wrapper over bool, int64_t, double, and std::string with helpers to convert to/from crow::json and to access/set values with automatic type normalization (wrap_mv_t).
Tracks key expirations using a sorted set of (time,key) and a map for quick updates/removals. Provides peek/pop for earliest expiration and iteration over scheduled expirations.

Shared, per-session cache node used across requests. Holds session ID, pending requested ID, key->multi_value entries, a dirty-key set, store-specific data pointer, refresh flag, reference count, and a recursive mutex for synchronization.
Simple in-memory session store mapping session_id to a map of key->multi_value. load moves stored entries into the CachedSession; save moves entries back. Not persistent across process restarts.

Filesystem-backed session store. Persists each session as a JSON file under a folder, tracks expirations using ExpirationTracker, evicts expired sessions, and writes a sidecar .expirations file on destruction.

Middleware-like struct in the crow namespace that ensures HTTP responses have a UTF-8 Content-Type if none is already set. Provides empty context type and two hooks: before_handle (no-op) and after_handle (sets default Content-Type). Intended for use in a middleware chain.

TCP listening acceptor wrapper for crow using Asio. Holds an asio tcp::acceptor and provides helpers to get port/address, URL display, and access to the underlying acceptor. Constructed with an asio::io_context. Reuse-address is enabled via reuse_address_option().

Alias type for error codes used by crow. It resolves to boost::system::error_code when CROW_USE_BOOST is defined, otherwise to asio::error_code. Only referenced here; no definition in this header.

functions.name: CROW_ROUTE
functions.description: Macro to declare an HTTP route on an application instance. Expands to a templated call that selects a rule type based on the URL pattern at compile time, enabling parameter extraction. Typical use: CROW_ROUTE(app, "/path")(handler...).
requirements: app must be a Crow application object (e.g., crow::SimpleApp or crow::App<...>).
url should be a route pattern understood by Crow (string literal or std::string) and compatible with crow::black_magic::get_parameter_tag.
The macro must be followed by a callable (e.g., lambda) of a signature compatible with the route’s parameters and return type expected by Crow.

functions.name: CROW_BP_ROUTE
functions.description: Macro to declare an HTTP route on a crow::Blueprint. Works like CROW_ROUTE but targets a blueprint object, enabling compile-time route tagging and parameter extraction.
requirements: blueprint must be a crow::Blueprint instance.
url must be a valid Crow route pattern compatible with crow::black_magic::get_parameter_tag.
Must be followed by a callable handler compatible with the route’s parameter arity/types.

functions.name: CROW_WEBSOCKET_ROUTE
functions.description: Macro to declare a WebSocket route on an application instance and obtain a WebSocket route configurator. Handlers for onopen/onclose/onmessage can be chained on the result.
requirements: app must be a Crow application object (e.g., crow::SimpleApp or crow::App<...>).
url must be a valid Crow route pattern for WebSockets.
The resulting object expects chained configuration: .onopen(...), .onclose(...), .onmessage(...), with callable signatures as required by Crow’s websocket API.
The address and port must be appropriately configured before server run for the endpoint to be reachable.

functions.name: CROW_MIDDLEWARES
functions.description: Macro to attach one or more middleware types to a specific route declaration. Use in a route-building chain before the handler to enable per-route middleware.
requirements: Use within a route definition chain (e.g., CROW_ROUTE(...).CROW_MIDDLEWARES(app, MW1, MW2)(handler)).
Each middleware type in ... must satisfy Crow’s middleware interface and be available to the translation unit.
app must be the crow::App/ SimpleApp instance used for the route.

functions.name: CROW_CATCHALL_ROUTE
functions.description: Macro to access the application’s catchall rule and define a handler for unrouted requests. Useful to customize 404-like behavior.
requirements: app must be a Crow application object.
Must be followed by assigning a handler compatible with Crow’s rule API (e.g., operator() with a handler).

functions.name: CROW_BP_CATCHALL_ROUTE
functions.description: Macro to access a blueprint’s catchall rule and define a handler for unrouted requests within that blueprint’s scope.
requirements: blueprint must be a crow::Blueprint instance.
Must be followed by a handler compatible with the blueprint’s rule API.

functions.name: crow::Crow::handle_upgrade
functions.signature: template<typename Adaptor> void handle_upgrade(const request& req, response& res, Adaptor&& adaptor)
functions.description: Process an HTTP Upgrade request, delegating to the router to perform protocol upgrades (e.g., WebSocket handshakes).
requirements: req must reference a valid, parsed crow::request containing an Upgrade request.
res must be a valid crow::response associated with the same connection lifecycle.
adaptor must be a valid network adaptor compatible with Crow’s server stack and valid for the duration of the call.

functions.name: crow::Crow::handle_initial
functions.description: Perform initial routing using only the HTTP method and URL, returning a routing_handle_result describing the matched rule (or catchall) or an error response.
requirements: req and res must be valid references for the duration of the call.
Caller should check the returned pointer for non-null and inspect fields (e.g., rule_index, catch_all) to decide next steps.
If an error response is set in res (no route), caller should not proceed to full handling.

functions.name: crow::Crow::handle
functions.signature: void handle(request& req, response& res, std::unique_ptr<routing_handle_result>& found)
functions.description: Complete request handling after initial routing, invoking the matched route handler to generate a response.
requirements: found must be a non-null routing_handle_result produced by handle_initial for the same req.
req and res must remain valid for the entire call.
Caller should ensure found indicates a valid target (e.g., found->rule_index or found->catch_all) before calling (as implied by handle_full).

functions.name: crow::Crow::handle_full
functions.description: Convenience method to perform both initial routing and full handling start-to-finish, primarily for debugging.
requirements: req and res must be valid for the duration of the call.
Intended for debugging; in production servers the standard flow is via the server loop.

functions.name: crow::Crow::route_dynamic
functions.description: Create a dynamic route rule at runtime. Prefer using CROW_ROUTE for compile-time tagged routes.
requirements: rule must be a valid Crow route pattern string.
Caller must attach a compatible handler to the returned DynamicRule before running the server.

functions.name: crow::Crow::route
functions.signature: template<uint64_t Tag> auto route(const std::string& rule) -> typename std::invoke_result<decltype(&Router::new_rule_tagged<Tag>), Router, const std::string&>::type
functions.description: Create a compile-time tagged route corresponding to rule, enabling parameter extraction and type safety. Usually invoked via CROW_ROUTE.
requirements: Tag is provided by crow::black_magic::get_parameter_tag(url) in normal usage.
rule must be a valid route pattern compatible with Tag.
Caller must attach a handler whose signature matches the inferred path parameters.

functions.name: crow::Crow::catchall_route
functions.description: Access the application’s catchall rule for handling requests that do not match any defined route.
requirements: Caller must assign a handler to the returned CatchallRule before requests are processed to customize behavior.

functions.name: crow::Crow::websocket_max_payload
functions.description: Set the default maximum WebSocket message payload size for connections created by this app.
requirements: max_payload must fit in uint64_t; values represent bytes.
Call before starting the server to affect new connections.

functions.name: crow::Crow::websocket_max_payload

functions.name: crow::ci_hash::operator()
functions.description: Case-insensitive hash functor for strings, intended for use with crow::ci_map (an unordered_multimap). This functor is stateless and may be invoked concurrently from multiple threads.

functions.name: crow::method_name
functions.description: Return the canonical uppercase HTTP method name string for a given crow::HTTPMethod. If the value is outside the defined range, returns the literal "invalid". Typical use is for logging, diagnostics, or building protocol text.
requirements: Argument method should be a valid enumerator less than crow::HTTPMethod::InternalMethodCount to obtain a real method name; otherwise the function returns "invalid".

functions.name: method_from_string
functions.description: Map a null-terminated C string containing an uppercase HTTP method token to its corresponding crow::HTTPMethod. If the token is not recognized, throws std::runtime_error("invalid http method"). Can be used in constant expressions when given a matching string literal. Defined only when CROW_MSVC_WORKAROUND is not defined.
requirements: Available only when CROW_MSVC_WORKAROUND is not defined (function is enclosed in #ifndef CROW_MSVC_WORKAROUND).
Argument str must be a non-null pointer to a null-terminated C string.

The string must exactly match one of the supported tokens (case-sensitive): "GET", "DELETE", "HEAD", "POST", "PUT", "OPTIONS", "CONNECT", "TRACE", "PATCH", "PURGE", "COPY", "LOCK", "MKCOL", "MOVE", "PROPFIND", "PROPPATCH", "SEARCH", "UNLOCK", "BIND", "REBIND", "UNBIND", "ACL", "REPORT", "MKACTIVITY", "CHECKOUT", "MERGE", "MSEARCH", "NOTIFY", "SUBSCRIBE", "UNSUBSCRIBE", "MKCALENDAR", "LINK", "UNLINK", "SOURCE".
If the input does not match any supported token, the function throws std::runtime_error; callers must either ensure valid input or handle the exception.
When used in a constant expression, the input must be a string literal (or otherwise constexpr-evaluable) matching a supported token; otherwise constant evaluation will fail.

functions.name: operator""_method
functions.signature: constexpr crow::HTTPMethod operator""_method(const char* str, size_t len)
functions.description: User-defined literal that converts a string literal HTTP method token to crow::HTTPMethod by delegating to method_from_string. Intended usage: "GET"_method, "POST"_method, etc. Throws std::runtime_error at runtime if the token is unrecognized. Defined only when CROW_MSVC_WORKAROUND is not defined.
requirements: Available only when CROW_MSVC_WORKAROUND is not defined (operator is enclosed in #ifndef CROW_MSVC_WORKAROUND).
Must be used with a string literal or literal operator call site providing a null-terminated sequence; the len parameter is ignored by the implementation.

The literal content must exactly match one of the supported tokens (case-sensitive): "GET", "DELETE", "HEAD", "POST", "PUT", "OPTIONS", "CONNECT", "TRACE", "PATCH", "PURGE", "COPY", "LOCK", "MKCOL", "MOVE", "PROPFIND", "PROPPATCH", "SEARCH", "UNLOCK", "BIND", "REBIND", "UNBIND", "ACL", "REPORT", "MKACTIVITY", "CHECKOUT", "MERGE", "MSEARCH", "NOTIFY", "SUBSCRIBE", "UNSUBSCRIBE", "MKCALENDAR", "LINK", "UNLINK", "SOURCE".

If the literal does not match any supported token, method_from_string will throw std::runtime_error; callers must ensure valid tokens at compile time for constexpr use or handle exceptions at runtime.

functions.name: crow::compression::compress_string
functions.signature: inline std::string crow::compression::compress_string(std::string const& str, crow::compression::algorithm algo)
functions.description: Compresses the given string using zlib deflate. The algorithm parameter selects the zlib windowBits mode: DEFLATE (zlib wrapper) or GZIP (gzip wrapper). Internally calls deflateInit2 with Z_DEFAULT_COMPRESSION and streams the data through a fixed 8KB buffer until completion. Returns the compressed data on success, or an empty string on failure (e.g., initialization failure or streaming error). Intended for compressing arbitrary binary/text payloads for transport or storage.
requirements: This function is only available when compiled with CROW_ENABLE_COMPRESSION defined.
Requires zlib at compile/link time (uses deflateInit2/deflate/deflateEnd).
Parameter algo must be a valid crow::compression::algorithm value (DEFLATE or GZIP), corresponding to zlib windowBits values for deflateInit2.
Input str may contain arbitrary binary data; it is not modified.
Caller should treat an empty return value as a compression failure (this implementation clears the output if the deflate stream does not end with Z_STREAM_END).
The function is reentrant and thread-safe as it uses only local state.

functions.name: crow::compression::decompress_string
functions.description: Decompresses data produced by zlib/deflate or gzip and returns the inflated string. Internally initializes zlib with automatic header detection (MAX_WBITS | 32) and streams via an 8KB buffer until inflate completes or an error occurs. On inflate errors, it returns an empty string; on success, it returns the decompressed bytes (which may legitimately be empty if the original content was empty). Suitable for reversing data compressed with compress_string(GZIP) or DEFLATE, or other compatible deflate/gzip sources.
requirements: This function is only available when compiled with CROW_ENABLE_COMPRESSION defined.
Requires zlib at compile/link time (uses inflateInit2/inflate/inflateEnd).
Input deflated_string must be valid zlib/deflate or gzip data; otherwise the function returns an empty string.

Return value note: an empty string can indicate either a successful decompression of empty content or a failure during inflate; callers that must distinguish these cases need additional validation or metadata.
Input may contain arbitrary binary data; it is not modified by the library (despite internal const_cast for zlib API).
The function is reentrant and thread-safe as it uses only local state.

functions.name: crow::bad_request::bad_request

Can be thrown and caught as crow::bad_request or as std::runtime_error.

functions.name: crow::bad_request::bad_request

Can be thrown and caught as crow::bad_request or as std::runtime_error.

functions.signature:
template <typename Adaptor, typename Handler, typename... Middlewares>
decltype(std::declval<Adaptor>().raw_socket())& crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::socket()

functions.name: crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::start
functions.signature:
template <typename Adaptor, typename Handler, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::start()
functions.description: Begins processing on the connection by starting the adaptor, arming the deadline timer, clearing the HTTP parser, and initiating the first async read. Intended as the entry point after constructing a Connection.
requirements: Should be called to initiate I/O on a newly constructed Connection (typically once per Connection).
Requires the underlying adaptor to be constructible/initialized (satisfied by the constructor).
On adaptor start failure, the function logs an error and does not proceed with reading.

functions.name: crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::handle_url
functions.signature:
template <typename Adaptor, typename Handler, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::handle_url()
functions.description: Invokes the handler’s initial routing decision for the parsed request URL and method. If no route is found for the method (no rule_index and not catch_all), terminates parsing early and completes the request immediately.
requirements: Should be called after the request URL and method are parsed and available in req_.
If no route is matched, the function marks the parser done and triggers response completion without further processing.

functions.name: crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::handle_header
functions.signature:
template <typename Adaptor, typename Handler, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::handle_header()
functions.description: Processes parsed request headers for connection-level directives. Specifically, if the client sent HTTP/1.1 with Expect: 100-continue, sends a synchronous 100 Continue interim response before the body is read.
requirements: Should be called after headers are parsed and before the request body is processed.
Only sends 100 Continue when HTTP/1.1 and the Expect header equals "100-continue".
Performs synchronous write on the connection; caller must tolerate that this may fail (errors are logged).

functions.name: crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::handle
functions.signature:
template <typename Adaptor, typename Handler, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::handle()
functions.description: Main request handler entry after parsing. Cancels the deadline timer, initializes middleware context, validates HTTP/1.1 Host header, handles protocol upgrades (e.g., non-h2 Upgrade), invokes global middleware, and dispatches to the handler. If the response completes immediately, it is sent; otherwise, completion is deferred until the handler calls the provided completion callback.
requirements: Requires req_ to be populated by the parser (HTTP version, headers, URL, method set).
If HTTP/1.1, requests without a Host header are treated as invalid and responded to with 400 (no special caller action required other than providing a valid Host header).
If the request has an Upgrade header not starting with "h2", the connection is handed off via handler_->handle_upgrade and the connection will be closed afterward.
Middleware tuple (middlewares_) must be valid (provided at construction).
The underlying adaptor must be open; otherwise, subsequent I/O will fail and the connection will be closed.

functions.name: crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::complete_request
functions.signature:
template <typename Adaptor, typename Handler, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Connection<Adaptor, Handler, Middlewares...>::complete_request()
functions.description: Finalizes and sends the HTTP response. Runs after-handler middleware (if pending), optionally compresses the body based on server settings and Accept-Encoding, prepares headers/buffers, and writes the response. Uses a static file transfer path when the response is static; otherwise streams the body with threshold-based behavior, then closes the connection if required.
requirements: Should be called after the handler has prepared crow::response (status, headers, body).
If after-handlers were scheduled, they are invoked exactly once before sending.
Compression is applied only when enabled by the handler and accepted by the client (Accept-Encoding) and when res.compressed is true.
For static responses, res.file_info must describe a valid readable file for full transfer; errors are logged if writes fail.
May close the connection depending on Connection’s close flag; callers should not assume keep-alive unless set.

functions.name: crow::parse_url_char
functions.signature: crow::state crow::parse_url_char(crow::state s, const char ch, crow::http_parser* parser, const char* url_mark, const char* p)
functions.description: Advance the HTTP request-target URL parsing state machine by one character. Given the current URL-parse state, the next input character, and parser/context pointers, returns the next state or s_dead on error. Intended to be called from http_parser_execute() for validating and splitting request URLs; callers should only feed non-whitespace characters. It also records the query-string start offset in parser->qs_point when encountering '?'.
requirements: s must be a valid state for URL parsing (e.g., s_req_spaces_before_url, s_req_schema, s_req_server, s_req_path, s_req_query_string_start, s_req_query_string).
ch must not be a whitespace character (space, CR, LF, TAB, FF); function is documented to only be invoked with non-space characters.
parser must be a valid, initialized crow::http_parser pointer.

When s is one of: s_req_server_start, s_req_server, s_req_server_with_at, s_req_path, s_req_query_string_start, or s_req_query_string, url_mark must point to the start of the URL within the same buffer as p, and p must be a position within or after url_mark (function computes p - url_mark).
p must point to the current character location within the input buffer corresponding to ch.
On returning s_dead, the caller should treat it as a URL parsing error (e.g., set CHPE_INVALID_URL as http_parser_execute does).

functions.name: crow::http_parser_execute
functions.signature: size_t crow::http_parser_execute(crow::http_parser* parser, const crow::http_parser_settings* settings, const char* data, size_t len)
functions.description: Incrementally parses an HTTP/1.x request from the given byte buffer, driving user-provided callbacks as parts of the message are recognized. Returns the number of bytes successfully consumed. On error or pause (callback returns non-zero), it stops and returns the number of bytes processed so far, with parser->http_errno indicating the reason. Supports chunked transfer-encoding, Content-Length, and HTTP/0.9 GET. Special handling exists for on_headers_complete: returning 1 means no body is expected; returning 2 means no body and no further messages (e.g., CONNECT).
requirements: parser must be a valid crow::http_parser pointer; typically initialize it with crow::http_parser_init() before first use.

settings may be null or may have any subset of callbacks set; each callback, if set, must conform to the declared type and return 0 on success or non-zero to signal an error/pause. The recognized callbacks are: on_message_begin, on_method, on_url, on_header_field, on_header_value, on_headers_complete, on_body, on_message_complete.
data must point to a valid memory buffer of at least len bytes; len may be zero.
If len is zero: only certain states are allowed (e.g., s_body_identity_eof leads to on_message_complete); otherwise CHPE_INVALID_EOF_STATE may be set and 1 returned.

Caller must check parser->http_errno (via CROW_HTTP_PARSER_ERRNO(parser)) after return to determine success (CHPE_OK) vs error; also check parser->upgrade flag when return occurs to detect protocol upgrade.
Callbacks must not assume data chunking boundaries; data callbacks may be invoked multiple times for a single logical field or body.

on_headers_complete may return: 0 normally; 1 to indicate no body is expected; 2 to indicate no body and terminate further messages (sets parser->upgrade=1). Other return values set CHPE_CB_headers_complete and stop parsing.

If both Transfer-Encoding (set) and Content-Length are present in the headers: in strict mode (lenient_http_headers==0) this is an error (CHPE_UNEXPECTED_CONTENT_LENGTH) unless TE is chunked and allow_chunked_length is set; in lenient mode, behavior follows RFC rules (may switch to s_body_identity_eof).
When parser->flags has F_SKIPBODY set (e.g., due to HEAD handling), the parser will skip body parsing and call on_message_complete after headers.
Function is not guaranteed to parse an entire message if len is insufficient; caller should provide remaining bytes in subsequent calls, preserving parser across calls.

functions.name: crow::http_parser_init
functions.description: Initializes an http_parser for parsing a new HTTP request. Resets all fields to defaults and sets the starting state to s_start_req while preserving the application-owned parser->data pointer.
requirements: parser must be a non-null pointer to crow::http_parser storage.

If parser->data contains application context, it is preserved; all other fields are zeroed, state set to s_start_req, and http_errno set to CHPE_OK. Call before first use or to reuse a parser for a new message stream.

Returns a pointer to a static string; the caller must not free or modify it.

functions.name: crow::http_errno_description
functions.description: Returns a human-readable description string for the specified http-parser error code, e.g., "invalid HTTP method". Intended for logging and diagnostics.
requirements: err must be a valid value of crow::http_errno; the function asserts that err is within range of the internal lookup table.

functions.name: crow::get_header_value
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
inline const std::string& crow::get_header_value(const T& headers, const std::string& key)
functions.description: Lookup a case-sensitive key in a header-like container and return the associated value by reference. If the key is not present, returns a reference to a static empty string. Intended for map-like containers holding std::string values. Usage: pass a container that supports count(key) and find(key)->second and a header name to retrieve.

The returned reference refers to either the element stored in headers (valid as long as the element remains in the container) or a static empty string with static storage duration
The returned reference is const; callers must not attempt to modify it

functions.name: crow::request::add_header
functions.description: Insert a header field into the request's header map (ci_map) using emplace. Useful for programmatically augmenting the request headers (e.g., during middleware processing).

handler must satisfy Asio’s CompletionHandler requirements: callable, movable (and usually copy-constructible), and invocable with no arguments

functions.name: crow::Server::Server
functions.signature:
template <typename Handler, typename Acceptor = TCPAcceptor, typename Adaptor = SocketAdaptor, typename... Middlewares>
crow::Server<Handler, Acceptor, Adaptor, Middlewares...>::Server(
    Handler* handler,
    typename Acceptor::endpoint endpoint,
    std::string server_name = std::string("Crow/") + VERSION,
    std::tuple<Middlewares...>* middlewares = nullptr,
    unsigned int concurrency = 1,
    uint8_t timeout = 5,
    typename Adaptor::context* adaptor_ctx = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs a Crow HTTP server bound to the given endpoint, preparing acceptor and I/O infrastructure. It opens, sets options on, binds, and listens on the acceptor, recording any startup failure. The handler and optional middleware/context pointers are stored for later use in run(). Use this to configure server characteristics (server name, concurrency, timeouts) before calling run(). Note: if initialization fails, startup_failed_ is set and later run() will abort.
requirements: handler must be a valid non-null pointer; it is dereferenced in run().
endpoint must be a valid endpoint for the chosen Acceptor; binding must succeed for the server to start.
If binding/opening/listening fails, the constructor logs and marks startup as failed; callers should check behavior via run() (which will early-exit) or by attempting to use the server.
concurrency is used as (concurrency - 1) worker threads; to avoid out-of-range access during acceptance, concurrency must be >= 2 (inferred from indexing into worker pools).
timeout is an 8-bit value used for task timer default timeout; specific range semantics beyond uint8_t are unknown.
middlewares and adaptor_ctx may be null; they are passed along to connections as-is.

functions.name: crow::Server::set_tick_function
functions.signature:
template <typename Handler, typename Acceptor = TCPAcceptor, typename Adaptor = SocketAdaptor, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Server<Handler, Acceptor, Adaptor, Middlewares...>::set_tick_function(std::chrono::milliseconds d, std::function<void()> f)
functions.description: Sets a periodic tick function and interval. When enabled (and run() is called), the function f will be invoked repeatedly every d milliseconds on the server's main io_context via an asynchronous timer. Use to schedule lightweight periodic tasks (e.g., housekeeping).
requirements: d specifies the interval between invocations; must be non-negative; zero or negative values will disable scheduling unless on_tick() is called manually (interval check occurs in run()).

f must be a valid callable; it will be invoked without arguments on the io_context thread. It should be fast and exception-safe to avoid stalling the event loop (inferred from asynchronous timer usage).

functions.name: crow::Server::on_tick
functions.signature:
template <typename Handler, typename Acceptor = TCPAcceptor, typename Adaptor = SocketAdaptor, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Server<Handler, Acceptor, Adaptor, Middlewares...>::on_tick()
functions.description: Executes the configured tick function once and reschedules the next invocation based on the current tick interval. Normally called internally by the timer started in run(). Public exposure allows manual triggering if desired.
requirements: Must only be called after set_tick_function() has been used to set a valid function; otherwise dereferencing a null callable will result in undefined behavior (inferred from direct call to tick_function_()).
Should be called in the context of the server's io_context thread if manual invocation is used, to preserve thread-affinity with other asynchronous operations (inferred).

functions.name: crow::Server::run
functions.signature:
template <typename Handler, typename Acceptor = TCPAcceptor, typename Adaptor = SocketAdaptor, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Server<Handler, Acceptor, Adaptor, Middlewares...>::run()
functions.description: Starts the server: initializes worker io_contexts and task timers, starts periodic tick handling if configured, begins accepting connections, installs asynchronous signal handling, and enters the main event loop. This call blocks the calling thread until shutdown (it spawns a thread to run the main io_context and immediately joins it). If construction failed, run() logs and returns immediately.
requirements: Constructor must have succeeded (no startup_failed_); otherwise run() returns without starting.
handler must be valid (non-null); run() dereferences handler to set port/address information.
concurrency must be >= 2 so that at least one worker io_context exists for connection handling; otherwise acceptance/dispatch will access empty pools (inferred from indexing logic).
If set_tick_function() was used, tick interval must be > 0 to enable scheduling; otherwise on_tick() will not be armed automatically.
run() should typically be called once for a given Server instance; calling after stop() without reinitialization may not be supported (not specified).

functions.name: crow::Server::stop
functions.signature:
template <typename Handler, typename Acceptor = TCPAcceptor, typename Adaptor = SocketAdaptor, typename... Middlewares>
void crow::Server<Handler, Acceptor, Adaptor, Middlewares...>::stop()
functions.description: Initiates server shutdown: prevents new accepts, closes the acceptor, stops all worker io_contexts and the main io_context. Intended to be called from signal handlers or application logic to shut down cleanly.
requirements: May be called at any time; if the acceptor is open it will be closed, with errors logged but otherwise ignored.
It is safe to call multiple times; subsequent calls will find the acceptor already closed (inferred from checks).

Active operations on io_contexts are stopped; callers should ensure any required cleanup dependent on outstanding operations is handled externally if necessary (not specified beyond io_context::stop()).

functions.name: crow::ILogHandler::log
functions.signature: virtual void crow::ILogHandler::log(const std::string& message, crow::LogLevel level) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual hook that writes a single log message at the given severity level. Implement this in a custom log handler to route messages (e.g., to stderr, files, syslog). It is invoked by crow::logger (notably from crow::logger’s destructor) when logging is enabled and the message’s level passes the current threshold.
requirements: Must be implemented by any concrete ILogHandler subclass.
Must be callable from crow::logger’s destructor; implementations should not throw exceptions (throwing during a destructor call leads to std::terminate). [inferred from usage]
Should handle arbitrary message contents (including empty strings).
No ownership of the message string; do not store references beyond the call unless copied.
Thread-safety: unknown (not specified). If used from multiple threads, the implementation should be made thread-safe as needed. [unknown]

functions.name: crow::logger::logger
functions.description: Constructs a logger for a specific severity level. Messages streamed into this logger (via operator<<) are buffered and, upon destruction, conditionally emitted through the current ILogHandler if CROW_ENABLE_LOGGING is defined and the level meets or exceeds the current log level.
requirements: Parameter level must be a valid crow::LogLevel enumerator.
No side effects occur unless CROW_ENABLE_LOGGING is defined; otherwise it acts as a no-op buffer.
The associated handler (set via setHandler) must be non-null and valid at destruction time if logging occurs. [inferred from usage]

functions.name: crow::logger::~logger
functions.description: Destructor that finalizes the log entry. If CROW_ENABLE_LOGGING is defined and this logger’s level is >= the current global log level, it forwards the accumulated message to the active ILogHandler via ILogHandler::log.
requirements: If logging occurs, a valid non-null handler must be installed via setHandler; otherwise dereferencing a null handler would result in undefined behavior. [inferred from code]
I/O from the handler must not throw exceptions; exceptions escaping the destructor will cause std::terminate. [inferred from destructor semantics]
Destruction may perform I/O (e.g., writing to stderr), so avoid calling it in contexts where such side effects are prohibited.

functions.name: crow::logger::operator<<
functions.signature: template <typename T> crow::logger& crow::logger::operator<<(T const& value)
functions.description: Streams a value into the logger’s internal std::ostringstream buffer. When the logger is later destroyed, the buffered content may be emitted depending on the log level and compile-time settings. If CROW_ENABLE_LOGGING is not defined or the logger’s level is below the current threshold, it still returns itself but does not append to the buffer.
requirements: Type T must be stream-insertable into std::ostringstream (i.e., the expression (std::ostringstream&) << value is well-formed).
No lifetime constraints on value beyond the call; the content is copied into the stream.
Behavior is gated by CROW_ENABLE_LOGGING and the current log level threshold; if disabled or filtered, insertion is effectively ignored.

functions.name: crow::logger::setLogLevel
functions.description: Sets the process-wide current log level threshold. Only messages with a level >= this setting will be emitted when CROW_ENABLE_LOGGING is defined.
requirements: Parameter level must be a valid crow::LogLevel enumerator.
Affects subsequent logging operations globally; existing logger instances compare against the updated threshold at destruction time.
Thread-safety: unknown; concurrent calls without external synchronization may race. [unknown]

functions.name: crow::logger::setHandler
functions.description: Installs the global log handler used by crow::logger to emit messages. By default, a CerrLogHandler is used, which writes to std::cerr with timestamps and level tags.
requirements: handler must be non-null. The implementation dereferences the pointer without null checks. [inferred from code]
The handler object must remain alive and valid until replaced by another valid handler or until all logger instances that may use it have been destroyed. [inferred from usage]
Ownership is not transferred; caller is responsible for managing the handler’s lifetime.
Handler’s log method should not throw (calls can occur from destructors). [inferred from usage]
Thread-safety: unknown; replacing the handler concurrently with logging may race without external synchronization. [unknown]

functions.name: crow::logger::get_current_log_level
functions.description: Returns the current global log level threshold used to decide whether messages are emitted when logging is enabled.
requirements: None beyond general preconditions of static function call.
Return value is a crow::LogLevel; callers should compare message levels using >= to decide if logging will occur (consistent with internal checks).

functions.name: crow::multipart::get_header_value_object
functions.signature:
template <typename O, typename T>
inline const O& crow::multipart::get_header_value_object(const T& headers, const std::string& key)
functions.description: Generic utility to look up a header-like value object by key in a header container. If the key exists, returns a const reference to the associated value; otherwise returns a const reference to a static default-constructed O. Intended for containers that provide count(key) and find(key).
requirements: Template parameter O must be default-constructible (the function returns a reference to a static default O when the key is not found).
The headers argument must support headers.count(key) and headers.find(key)->second expressions (i.e., an associative container interface).
The returned reference may alias a function-local static object when the key is not present; callers must not attempt to modify it.
Key comparison and case sensitivity depend on the provided headers container (not enforced by this function).

functions.name: crow::multipart::get_header_object
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
inline const crow::multipart::header& crow::multipart::get_header_object(const T& headers, const std::string& key)
functions.description: Convenience wrapper around get_header_value_object specialized for multipart::header. Returns the header object for the given key if present, otherwise a const reference to a static default header.
requirements: The headers argument must be a header-like associative container with key of std::string and value of crow::multipart::header, and must support count(key) and find(key).
Returned reference may alias a function-local static default header when the key is not found; callers must not modify it.
Key comparison behavior (case sensitivity) depends on the provided headers container.

functions.name: crow::multipart::part::get_header_object
functions.description: Retrieves a header object from this part by key. Returns a const reference to the stored header if present, otherwise a const reference to a static default header.
requirements: Key should be a header name such as "Content-Disposition" or "Content-Type".
When the header is missing, the returned reference aliases a static default header; callers must not modify it.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message::get_header_value
functions.description: Returns the value string of a message-level header from this multipart message. Delegates to crow::get_header_value on the message's ci_map headers.
requirements: Key must refer to a header present in message.headers for a meaningful result; behavior when missing depends on crow::get_header_value (not defined here).
The returned reference is valid as long as the message object (and its headers) remain alive.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message::get_part_by_name
functions.description: Finds and returns the first part whose Content-Disposition header has a name parameter equal to the provided name. Returns a default-constructed part if not found.
requirements: Each part is indexed in part_map by the Content-Disposition "name" parameter; if parts were constructed without that parameter, lookup may be invalid or undefined at construction time (see constructors).
Returned part is by value; modifications do not affect the message’s internal storage.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message::dump
functions.description: Serializes all parts of the multipart message into a string, excluding the message-level headers. Each part is preceded by the boundary delimiter and rendered via dump(int).
requirements: message.boundary should be set to a non-empty boundary string for a valid serialization format; if empty, the method still emits delimiters based on the current boundary value.
All parts contained in the message will be serialized in order.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message::message
functions.signature: crow::multipart::message::message(const crow::ci_map& headers_, const std::string& boundary_, const std::vector<crow::multipart::part>& sections)
functions.description: Constructs a multipart::message from provided headers, boundary, and an explicit list of parts. Sets the content_type to multipart/form-data with the given boundary (if non-empty), stores parts, and builds part_map keyed by each part’s Content-Disposition name parameter.
requirements: headers_ should contain the message-level headers relevant to the multipart message.
boundary_ may be empty; if empty, content_type remains at the default set by the base class. The serialized form may be nonstandard if boundary is empty.

Each part in sections must contain a "Content-Disposition" header with a "name" parameter; otherwise accessing params.find("name")->second during construction causes undefined behavior (dereferencing end iterator).

functions.name: crow::multipart::message::message
functions.description: Constructs and parses a multipart::message from an HTTP request. Extracts the boundary from the Content-Type header, sets content_type, and parses the body into parts and part_map.
requirements: req.headers must include a Content-Type header with a boundary parameter (e.g., "multipart/form-data; boundary=..."), otherwise this constructor throws crow::bad_request("Empty boundary in multipart message").
req.body must be a well-formed multipart payload using CRLF (\r\n) line endings and the extracted boundary. If the delimiter is not found or the body is ill-formed, parsing throws crow::bad_request.

Each part in the payload must include a "Content-Disposition" header with a "name" parameter; otherwise construction/parsing will dereference a non-existent parameter and result in undefined behavior.
Input must use proper header formatting: headers terminated by CRLF and a blank line (CRLF CRLF) between headers and body of each part.

functions.name: crow::multipart::get_header_object
functions.signature: const crow::multipart::header_view& crow::multipart::get_header_object(const crow::multipart::mph_view_map& headers, const std::string_view key)
functions.description: Finds a multipart header by key in the provided header multimap and returns it. If not found, returns a reference to a static, empty header_view. Useful for retrieving header metadata like Content-Type or Content-Disposition parameters when parsing multipart parts.
requirements: headers must reference a valid crow::multipart::mph_view_map during the call.
key may be any string; lookup is performed using the container’s comparator (case-insensitive per mph_view_map’s ci_hash/ci_key_eq).
The returned reference may refer to a static empty header_view if key is not found; callers must be able to handle an empty value/params.

functions.name: crow::multipart::padded::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& stream, const crow::multipart::padded value_)
functions.description: Streams the given padded string_view to the output stream, surrounding it with the specified padding character (double quote by default). Intended to format header parameter values like name fields in Content-Disposition.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable std::ostream.
value_.value must remain valid for the duration of the stream insertion call.
value_.padding is used verbatim; if it is not a quoting character, output will still be produced as padding-character + value + padding-character.

functions.name: crow::multipart::part_view::get_header_object
functions.description: Convenience accessor that retrieves a header_view from this part’s headers by key. Returns a static empty header_view if the key is not found.
requirements: this->headers must contain valid string_view keys/values while the function executes.
key may be any string; lookup follows mph_view_map’s comparator.
Callers must handle the case where an empty header_view is returned when the header is absent.

functions.name: crow::multipart::part_view::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& stream, const crow::multipart::part_view& part)
functions.description: Serializes a multipart part to the given stream, writing its headers (with parameters) followed by CRLF, an empty line, the body, and a trailing CRLF. Used when emitting multipart messages.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable std::ostream.
part.headers and all contained string_views (keys, header_view.value, parameter keys/values) must be valid during streaming.
part.body must be valid during streaming.
Output formatting relies on CRLF sequences and will include parameter values padded with double quotes via crow::multipart::padded.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message_view::get_header_value
functions.description: Returns the value of an HTTP header from the underlying request/response headers associated with this multipart message. Delegates to crow::get_header_value on the stored ci_map.
requirements: headers (the stored std::reference_wrapper<const ci_map>) must reference a valid ci_map.
key is the header field name; matching is subject to ci_map’s behavior (commonly case-insensitive).
Behavior when the header is missing depends on crow::get_header_value (unknown from this header); callers should be prepared for an empty return or library-defined behavior.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message_view::get_part_by_name
functions.description: Looks up and returns the first multipart part whose Content-Disposition name parameter matches the given name. If not found, returns a default-constructed part_view with empty headers/body.
requirements: name must be a valid string_view during the call.
part_map must be populated (e.g., via constructor or parse_body) for lookups to succeed.
Callers must handle the case where a default (empty) part_view is returned when no match is found.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message_view::operator<<
functions.signature: std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& stream, const crow::multipart::message_view message)
functions.description: Serializes the multipart message to the stream, writing boundary-delimited parts. It writes "--" + boundary, CRLF, each part, and finally the closing delimiter "--" + boundary + "--" followed by CRLF. Message-level headers are not included.
requirements: stream must be a valid, writable std::ostream.
message.boundary should be set appropriately for a valid MIME multipart; if empty, the output will still be produced with an empty boundary.
message.parts must contain valid parts; their internal string_views must remain valid during streaming.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message_view::dump
functions.description: Returns a string containing the serialized multipart body (all parts and boundaries), excluding any message-level HTTP headers. Internally streams the message into an ostringstream.
requirements: This function may allocate memory proportional to the serialized message size.
All part data and boundary must be valid and accessible for the duration of the call.

functions.name: crow::multipart::message_view::dump
functions.description: Returns a string containing the serialized representation of a single part (headers, blank line, body, and trailing CRLF). Uses parts.at(part_) and will throw std::out_of_range if the index is invalid.
requirements: part_ must be a valid zero-based index in [0, parts.size()).
May throw std::out_of_range if part_ is outside the valid range.
This function may allocate memory proportional to the serialized part size.

functions.name: crow::mustache::load
functions.description: Opens, sanitizes, reads, and compiles a mustache template file into a compiled template_t. Uses the current loader and template base directory, sanitizing the filename before reading. Throws if the template content is invalid.
requirements: filename is a path-like string; it will be sanitized via utility::sanitize_filename before loading
A loader must be set (default_loader is used by default) and must return the file contents as a std::string
If the template contains syntax errors or mismatched tags, an invalid_template_exception will be thrown during compilation
If the template uses partials ({{> name}}), the loader/environment must be able to load the referenced partial filename

functions.name: crow::mustache::template_t::render
functions.description: Renders the compiled mustache template with an empty context and returns a rendered_template (content-type text/html). Use when no dynamic data is needed.
requirements: The template_t must be a valid compiled template (constructed or produced via compile/load)
Rendering may throw if a tag resolves to an unsupported json::wvalue type or a partial fails to compile/load

functions.name: crow::mustache::template_t::render
functions.description: Renders the compiled mustache template using the provided context (json::wvalue) and returns a rendered_template (content-type text/html).
requirements: ctx must be a valid crow::json::wvalue (object, list, string, number, boolean, function, etc.) as expected by the template
If the template uses partials ({{> ...}}), those partials must be loadable via the current loader
Rendering may throw on unsupported value types for tags or if partial compilation fails

functions.name: crow::mustache::template_t::render_string
functions.description: Renders the compiled template using an empty context and returns the rendered output as a std::string (no returnable wrapper).
requirements: template_t must be valid/compiled
Rendering may throw if a tag resolves to an unsupported json::wvalue type or a partial fails to compile/load

functions.name: crow::mustache::template_t::render_string
functions.description: Renders the compiled template using the provided context (json::wvalue) and returns the output as a std::string.
requirements: ctx must be a valid crow::json::wvalue compatible with the template’s tags/sections
If the template uses partials, they must be loadable via the current loader
Rendering may throw on unsupported value types for tags or partial compilation failures

functions.name: crow::mustache::compile
functions.description: Compiles a mustache source string into a template_t by parsing tags, sections, partials, and delimiters. Prefer this over direct construction according to the documentation.
requirements: body must be a valid mustache template string; otherwise invalid_template_exception is thrown
Unmatched or malformed tags (e.g., {{# ... without {{/ ...}}) cause invalid_template_exception

functions.name: crow::mustache::default_loader
functions.description: Default file loader used by mustache load functions. Reads the file located under the current base directory and returns its contents. Logs a warning and returns an empty string if the file can’t be opened.
requirements: filename is joined with the current route-level base directory (set via set_base)
The process must have filesystem access permissions to read the target file
On failure it returns an empty string; callers relying on content should handle empty results

functions.name: crow::mustache::set_base
functions.description: Sets the route-level templates base directory (used by default_loader and friends). Ensures the stored base path ends with a path separator.
requirements: path must be non-empty; the implementation accesses path.back() and would be undefined for an empty string
Path may be updated at runtime; subsequent loads will use the new base directory

functions.name: crow::mustache::set_global_base
functions.description: Sets the global templates base directory (not tied to a blueprint). Ensures the stored base path ends with a path separator.
requirements: path must be non-empty; the implementation accesses path.back() and would be undefined for an empty string

functions.name: crow::mustache::set_loader
functions.description: Overrides the loader used by load/load_unsafe/load_text/load_text_unsafe. The provided callable is moved into internal storage and invoked with a filename to obtain file contents.
requirements: loader must be a valid callable that accepts a std::string (filename) and returns a std::string (file contents)
The callable should be safe to store and invoke later; it will be moved into internal storage

functions.name: crow::mustache::load_text
functions.description: Opens, reads, and returns a file as a std::string after sanitizing the filename. Uses the current loader.
requirements: filename is sanitized via utility::sanitize_filename before being passed to the loader
A loader must be set (default_loader by default) and should return the file contents

functions.name: crow::mustache::load_text_unsafe
functions.description: Opens and reads a file using the current loader without sanitizing the filename. Returns the raw file contents.
requirements: Caller is responsible for ensuring filename safety and validity (no sanitization is performed)
A loader must be set (default_loader by default) and should return the file contents

functions.name: crow::mustache::load_unsafe
functions.description: Opens, reads, and compiles a template file without sanitizing the filename. Equivalent to compile(loader(filename)).
requirements: Caller is responsible for ensuring filename safety and validity (no sanitization is performed)
Compilation may throw invalid_template_exception on malformed templates
If the template includes partials, they must be loadable via the current loader

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_message_begin
functions.description: http-parser callback invoked when a new HTTP message begins. Resets/initializes per-message state as needed by the underlying http_parser. Returns 0 to continue parsing.
requirements: The http_parser* must actually point to a crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance (object layout must match via inheritance).
Intended to be called by http_parser_execute via its settings; do not call directly in normal usage.
Must be executed in the context of an active parse cycle started by feed().

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_method
functions.description: http-parser callback invoked when the HTTP method is parsed. Updates req.method from the underlying parser’s method field. Returns 0 to continue parsing.
requirements: self_ must point to a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance.
Called by http_parser_execute; not intended for direct external invocation.
Requires that the parser has identified a valid HTTP method prior to this callback (as guaranteed by http_parser).

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_url
functions.signature:
template<typename Handler>
static int crow::HTTPParser<Handler>::on_url(http_parser* self_, const char* at, size_t length);
functions.description: http-parser callback for URL data. Appends the received URL fragment to req.raw_url, parses query parameters into req.url_params, derives req.url (path without query), and then triggers process_url() to let the handler react. Returns 0 to continue.
requirements: self_ must point to a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance.
at must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes valid for the duration of the call (as per http_parser contract).
Handler type must provide handle_url() callable via handler_->handle_url().
qs_point is expected to be set by the underlying parser indicating the start of the query string; if zero, entire raw_url is treated as path.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_header_field
functions.signature:
template<typename Handler>
static int crow::HTTPParser<Handler>::on_header_field(http_parser* self_, const char* at, size_t length);
functions.description: http-parser callback for an HTTP header field name fragment. Manages internal state to accumulate field/value pairs and pushes completed headers into req.headers. Returns 0 to continue.
requirements: self_ must point to a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance.
at must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes valid for the duration of the call.
Assumes callbacks arrive in valid order per http_parser (field/value alternation).
Not intended to be called directly; used via http_parser_execute.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_header_value
functions.signature:
template<typename Handler>
static int crow::HTTPParser<Handler>::on_header_value(http_parser* self_, const char* at, size_t length);
functions.description: http-parser callback for an HTTP header value fragment. Accumulates or starts a new header value based on internal state and pairing with the most recent header field. Returns 0 to continue.
requirements: self_ must point to a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance.
at must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes valid for the duration of the call.
Relies on a prior on_header_field call for pairing when starting a new header.
Used via http_parser_execute; not intended for direct external calls.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_headers_complete
functions.description: http-parser callback indicating all headers are parsed. Flushes any in-progress header field/value into req.headers, sets connection parameters (HTTP version, keep-alive/close, upgrade) via set_connection_parameters(), and notifies the handler via process_header(). Returns 0 to continue.
requirements: self_ must point to a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance.
Handler type must provide handle_header() callable via handler_->handle_header().
Should be invoked by http_parser_execute after all headers are parsed; do not call out of sequence.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_body
functions.signature:
template<typename Handler>
static int crow::HTTPParser<Handler>::on_body(http_parser* self_, const char* at, size_t length);
functions.description: http-parser callback for a chunk of the HTTP message body. Appends the chunk to req.body. Returns 0 to continue.
requirements: self_ must point to a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance.
at must point to a readable buffer of at least length bytes valid for the duration of the call.
Body size may be large; callers/handlers should account for memory growth as req.body is appended.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::on_message_complete
functions.description: http-parser callback fired when the complete HTTP message has been parsed. Marks message_complete = true and invokes process_message() to let the handler process the fully parsed request. Returns 0 to continue.
requirements: self_ must point to a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler> instance.
Handler type must provide handle() callable via handler_->handle().
Intended to be invoked by http_parser_execute at the correct time; not for manual external calls.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::HTTPParser
functions.description: Constructs an HTTPParser bound to a supplied Handler instance. Initializes the base http_parser state via http_parser_init(this).
requirements: handler must be a valid, non-null pointer to a Handler instance for the duration of the HTTPParser’s use.
Handler must implement methods handle_url(), handle_header(), and handle().
HTTPParser object must remain alive and not be moved in a way that breaks the http_parser base subobject layout while parsing is active.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::feed
functions.signature:
template<typename Handler>
bool crow::HTTPParser<Handler>::feed(const char* buffer, int length);
functions.description: Feeds raw bytes from a TCP socket buffer to the parser. Drives http_parser_execute with the class’s callback table to parse request components. Returns true if all provided bytes were consumed and no parser error occurred; returns false on parser error or if not all bytes were consumed.
requirements: If length > 0, buffer must be a valid pointer to at least length bytes of readable memory.
If message_complete is already true, feed() returns true without parsing; callers should avoid feeding further data after completion unless resetting via clear().
http_parser_execute must be allowed to call the static callbacks; the object must be a valid crow::HTTPParser<Handler>.
Errors are indicated by a false return (either http_errno != CHPE_OK or nparsed != length); callers should stop feeding on error.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::done
functions.description: Signals end-of-input to the parser by calling feed(nullptr, 0). Useful to finalize parsing when no more data is available.
requirements: Should be called after all input has been provided to ensure the parser processes any buffered state.
Safe to call multiple times; returns the result of feed(nullptr, 0).

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::clear
functions.description: Resets the parser and request state to begin parsing a new message. Clears headers/body accumulation, resets internal state flags, and sets the parser state to CROW_NEW_MESSAGE().
requirements: Should be called only when no parse is in progress (i.e., not concurrently with feed()).
Invalidates any references/pointers into the previous req contents.
After clear(), the object is ready to parse a new message; handler_ remains unchanged and must still be valid.

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::process_url
functions.description: Invokes handler_->handle_url() after URL parsing. Provides a hook for the owning handler to react to the URL becoming available.
requirements: handler_ must be a valid pointer to a Handler instance.
Handler must implement handle_url().
Should be called only after on_url has populated req.raw_url/url/url_params (normally done automatically by the parser).

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::process_header
functions.description: Invokes handler_->handle_header() after headers are complete. Provides a hook for the handler to react to completed header parsing.
requirements: handler_ must be valid.
Handler must implement handle_header().
Should be called after on_headers_complete has finalized headers (normally done automatically by the parser).

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::process_message
functions.description: Invokes handler_->handle() when the entire HTTP message has been parsed. Entry point for the handler’s main processing of the request.
requirements: handler_ must be valid.
Handler must implement handle().
Should be called after on_message_complete has marked message completion (normally done automatically by the parser).

functions.name: crow::HTTPParser::set_connection_parameters
functions.description: Derives and stores HTTP protocol/version and connection semantics from the underlying parser fields: sets req.http_ver_major/minor, req.keep_alive, req.close_connection, and req.upgrade based on http_major/http_minor/flags/upgrade.
requirements: Call after the HTTP version and connection headers have been parsed (normally invoked within on_headers_complete).
Relies on http_parser base fields http_major, http_minor, flags, and upgrade being populated by the parser.

functions.name: crow::qs_strncmp
functions.signature: int crow::qs_strncmp(const char* s, const char* qs, size_t n)
functions.description: Compares up to n characters of two URL-encoded strings, decoding '+' to space and `%HH` hex escapes during comparison. Intended for comparing a plain key against a query-string segment safely.
requirements: s must be a valid, readable, null-terminated C string.
qs must be a valid, readable, null-terminated C string.
n may be any size_t; only up to n characters are compared, with URL-decoding applied as needed.
If either string contains a '%' escape, two following hex digits are read; invalid hex in an escape is treated as a null terminator in comparison.

functions.name: crow::qs_parse
functions.signature: size_t crow::qs_parse(char* qs, char* qs_kv[], size_t qs_kv_size, bool parse_url = true)
functions.description: Parses a query string (or full URL when parse_url is true) into k/v substrings, storing pointers to each k/v pair in qs_kv. Decodes the value portions in-place (keys are left as-is). Returns the number of k/v entries found.
requirements: qs must point to a writable, null-terminated buffer; the function writes null terminators and decodes values in-place.
qs_kv must be a valid array of pointers with capacity qs_kv_size; entries will be set to point into qs.
qs_kv_size is the maximum number of k/v pairs to record; additional pairs (if present) are ignored.
If parse_url is true, qs may be a full URL; parsing starts after the first '?' (or returns 0 if neither '?' nor '#' is found).

requirements: qs must point to a writable, null-terminated buffer.

qs_kv must point to an array of pointers previously filled by qs_parse for the same underlying buffer.
qs_kv_size is the number of entries in qs_kv to search.

Returned pointer points into the original mutable buffer passed to qs_parse; it remains valid only while that buffer remains alive and unmodified.

functions.description: Extracts the nth key-value pair for a dictionary-like query parameter of the form `dict_name[subkey]=value` from a qs_parse-produced array. Returns a pair<subkey,value> as owning strings, or nullptr if not found.
requirements: dict_name must be a valid, null-terminated C string prefix to match (compared without URL-decoding).
qs_kv must be an array of pointers obtained from qs_parse on the same buffer.
qs_kv_size is the number of entries to scan.
nth selects the 0-based dictionary entry to return; must be >= 0.

functions.description: Non-destructively searches a raw URL or query string for key and copies the decoded value into val (up to val_len). Returns val on success, or NULL if key not present or value absent.
requirements: key must be a valid, null-terminated C string.

val_len should be > 0 to allow storing at least the terminating NUL; if 0, buffer cannot be written.
Decoding handles '+' and `%HH`; invalid `%` sequences terminate decoding at that point.
