functions.name: crow::detail::task_timer::task_timer
functions.description: Constructs a periodic scheduler that invokes queued tasks after a number of ticks. Each tick has length tick_length (default 1 second). The instance arms an internal waitable timer and re-schedules itself after each tick to process due tasks.
requirements: io_context must remain alive for the entire lifetime of the task_timer instance.
io_context must be actively run/poll on at least one thread for timers and tasks to execute (per Asio usage patterns).
tick_length is used as the granularity for scheduling; zero or very small values may cause very frequent wakeups (behavior per Asio timers).

functions.name: crow::detail::task_timer::~task_timer
functions.description: Destructor; cancels the internal timer to stop further ticks and task processing. Any outstanding async wait will be canceled.
requirements: After destruction, the instance must not be used.
Canceling the timer may cause pending handlers to observe an operation_aborted error (per Asio semantics). Ensure your application tolerates this.

functions.name: crow::detail::task_timer::cancel
functions.description: Cancels a previously scheduled task by its identifier, preventing it from being executed if it has not already run.
requirements: id must be the identifier returned by a prior call to schedule on the same task_timer instance.
If the task corresponding to id has already executed or was not scheduled on this instance, the call has no effect.
Do not reuse identifiers across different task_timer instances; identifiers are not globally unique and are reset when no tasks remain (per class behavior).

functions.name: crow::detail::task_timer::schedule
functions.description: Schedules task to run after the current default timeout (in ticks). Returns an identifier that can be used to cancel the task before it runs.
requirements: task must be a valid callable; passing an empty std::function will result in std::bad_function_call when executed.
The returned identifier is only meaningful for this task_timer instance and only until the task runs; using it with other instances or after execution is unsafe (per comments).
Tasks execute in the context of the Asio timer handler; ensure the task body is safe to run there and does not block the io_context thread for long.

functions.name: crow::detail::task_timer::set_default_timeout
functions.description: Sets the default number of ticks to wait for schedule(task) calls that do not specify an explicit timeout. Default is 5 ticks.
requirements: timeout is the number of ticks (0–255) used for future schedule(task) calls on this instance.

functions.name: crow::detail::task_timer::get_default_timeout
functions.description: Returns the current default timeout (in ticks) used when scheduling tasks without an explicit timeout.

functions.name: crow::detail::task_timer::get_tick_length
functions.description: Returns the duration of a single tick for this task_timer instance.

functions.name: crow::black_magic::is_parameter_tag_compatible
functions.signature: static inline bool crow::black_magic::is_parameter_tag_compatible(uint64_t a, uint64_t b)
functions.description: Compares two encoded route-parameter tag sequences for compatibility. Each tag sequence is a base-6 encoding of parameter kinds; the function recursively compares element-by-element (treating tag 5 as 4) to determine if the two sequences match in structure. Intended for runtime validation of route parameter lists.
requirements: Arguments a and b are 64-bit encodings produced by crow::black_magic::get_parameter_tag* utilities or equivalent encoding.
Returns true if both encodings represent the same sequence of parameter kinds; false otherwise.
No side effects or exceptions are thrown by this function.

functions.name: crow::black_magic::find_closing_tag_runtime
functions.signature: static inline unsigned crow::black_magic::find_closing_tag_runtime(const char* s, unsigned p)
functions.description: Scans a C-string starting at index p to find the next closing tag character '>' and returns its index. Throws if no matching '>' is found before the string terminator. Used for parsing route parameter placeholders like <int>.
requirements: Parameter s must be a valid, null-terminated C-string pointer.
Parameter p must be a valid index within s (0 <= p < strlen(s)+1).
Throws std::runtime_error("unmatched tag <") if no '>' is found before the end of the string.

functions.name: crow::black_magic::get_parameter_tag_runtime
functions.signature: static inline uint64_t crow::black_magic::get_parameter_tag_runtime(const char* s, unsigned p = 0)
functions.description: Parses a route pattern C-string and returns a compact base-6 encoding of parameter types found (e.g., <int>, <uint>, <float>/<double>, <str>/<string>, <path>). Non-parameter characters are skipped. Used to compute a signature for route parameters at runtime.
requirements: Parameter s must be a valid, null-terminated C-string.
Parameter p is the starting index; must be within the bounds of s.
Recognized placeholders are exactly: <int>, <uint>, <float>, <double>, <str>, <string>, <path>.
Throws std::runtime_error on unmatched '<' (no closing '>') or on any invalid parameter type token within '<' and '>'.

functions.name: crow::utility::get_element_by_type
functions.signature:
template <class T, class... Args>
T& crow::utility::get_element_by_type(std::tuple<Args...>& t)
functions.description: Returns a reference to the first element of a std::tuple whose type exactly matches T. Useful for retrieving by type from heterogeneous tuples without specifying an index.
requirements: The tuple type std::tuple<Args...> must contain at least one element whose type is exactly T (no automatic cv/ref decay).
If multiple elements of type T exist, the first one is returned.

t must be a valid tuple lvalue, as a T& is returned.

functions.name: crow::utility::base64encode
functions.signature: inline static std::string crow::utility::base64encode(const unsigned char* data, size_t size, const char* key = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/")
functions.description: Encodes a raw byte buffer into a Base64 string using the provided 64-character alphabet (standard by default). Handles input sizes not divisible by 3 via '=' padding.
requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
key must point to a 64-character alphabet string; passing a shorter string leads to out-of-bounds access (no validation performed).
Returns a string of length ((size + 2) / 3) * 4.

functions.signature: inline static std::string crow::utility::base64encode(std::string data, size_t size, const char* key = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/")
functions.description: Encodes the first size bytes of the provided string's contents into Base64 using the provided alphabet (standard by default). Convenience overload forwarding to the pointer-based encoder.
requirements: size must be less than or equal to data.size(); otherwise the function will read past the end of the string's buffer (undefined behavior).
key must be a 64-character Base64 alphabet.
Returns a string of length ((size + 2) / 3) * 4.

requirements: data must point to at least size bytes of readable memory.
Returns a string of length ((size + 2) / 3) * 4.

Returns a string of length ((size + 2) / 3) * 4.

requirements: size must be less than or equal to data.size(); larger values lead to out-of-bounds reads (undefined behavior).
Input should contain only valid Base64 characters, '-' and '_', and optional '=' padding; invalid characters map to 0 without error.

functions.name: crow::utility::sanitize_filename
functions.signature: inline static void crow::utility::sanitize_filename(std::string& data, char replacement = '_')
functions.description: Sanitizes a filename in-place to remove or replace potentially dangerous or invalid characters and reserved device names (e.g., CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) and directory traversal '..'. Also truncates names longer than 255 characters.

functions.name: crow::utility::random_alphanum
functions.description: Generates a pseudo-random alphanumeric string of the specified length using [0-9a-zA-Z]. Uses std::random_device to seed a Mersenne Twister engine per call.
requirements: size specifies the number of characters to generate; no upper bound enforced.

functions.name: crow::utility::join_path
functions.signature: inline static std::string crow::utility::join_path(std::string path, const std::string& fname)

functions.name: crow::utility::find_first_of

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::create
functions.signature:
template <typename Adaptor, typename Handler>
static void crow::websocket::Connection<Adaptor, Handler>::create(const crow::request& req, Adaptor adaptor, Handler* handler, uint64_t max_payload, const std::vector<std::string>& subprotocols, std::function<void(crow::websocket::connection&)> open_handler, std::function<void(crow::websocket::connection&, const std::string&, bool)> message_handler, std::function<void(crow::websocket::connection&, const std::string&, uint16_t)> close_handler, std::function<void(crow::websocket::connection&, const std::string&)> error_handler, std::function<void(const crow::request&, std::optional<crow::response>&, void**)> accept_handler, bool mirror_protocols)
functions.description: Factory that validates the HTTP Upgrade request, negotiates the WebSocket handshake (including subprotocol), optionally runs an accept handler to reject or customize the upgrade, then starts the WebSocket connection and registers it with the Handler.
requirements: req must include header Upgrade: websocket; otherwise the adaptor is closed and no connection is created.
Sec-WebSocket-Key must be present; Sec-WebSocket-Version is expected to be 13 (implied by the accept computation and typical RFC 6455 flow).
adaptor must be a valid, connected transport supporting socket(), get_io_context(), shutdown_readwrite(), close(), and address().
handler must be non-null and must implement add_websocket(std::shared_ptr<Connection<Adaptor,Handler>>) and remove_websocket(std::shared_ptr<Connection<Adaptor,Handler>>) (called internally).
max_payload sets the maximum accepted payload size in bytes; messages exceeding it will close the connection with MessageTooBig.
subprotocols may be empty; if mirror_protocols is true and the request included Sec-WebSocket-Protocol, that value is echoed.
accept_handler may be null; if provided and it sets a response, that response is written and the connection is not established.
Callbacks (open_handler, message_handler, close_handler, error_handler) may be empty/null; if provided, they must be callable with the specified signatures.
Ownership: adaptor is moved into the new Connection and must not be used by the caller after calling create().

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::dispatch
functions.signature:
template <typename CompletionHandler>
void crow::websocket::Connection<Adaptor, Handler>::dispatch(CompletionHandler&& handler)
functions.description: Schedules the provided callable to run on the connection’s I/O context, executing inline if appropriate per asio::dispatch semantics. The call is guarded by an internal weak anchor to avoid running after destruction.
requirements: CompletionHandler must be invocable with no arguments and must be movable (will be stored and invoked).
May be called from any thread; execution occurs on adaptor_.get_io_context() (inferred from implementation).

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::post

template <typename CompletionHandler>
void crow::websocket::Connection<Adaptor, Handler>::post(CompletionHandler&& handler)
functions.description: Posts the provided callable to the connection’s I/O context for asynchronous execution. The call is guarded by an internal weak anchor to avoid running after destruction.
requirements: CompletionHandler must be invocable with no arguments and must be movable.
May be called from any thread; execution occurs asynchronously on adaptor_.get_io_context().

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::send_ping
functions.description: Queues and sends a WebSocket Ping control frame with the given payload.

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::send_pong
functions.description: Queues and sends a WebSocket Pong control frame with the given payload, typically used as a response to Ping.

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::close
functions.signature: void crow::websocket::Connection<Adaptor, Handler>::close(std::string const& msg, uint16_t status_code) override
functions.description: Initiates a WebSocket close handshake: sends a Close frame with status code and reason, marks the connection for shutdown, and triggers the close handler when both sides have closed.
requirements: status_code should be a valid WebSocket close status (1000–4999 inclusive); avoid reserved codes such as 1005, 1006, 1015 as noted in comments.
Safe to call once to initiate closing; repeated invocations after a received close lead to immediate shutdown and handler invocation as per implementation.
msg may be any UTF-8 text (typical for reason strings) and is sent along with the 2-byte status code.

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::get_remote_ip
functions.description: Returns the remote peer IP address as reported by the underlying adaptor.
requirements: The adaptor must support address() and the connection must have been established.

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::set_max_payload_size
functions.description: Sets the maximum allowed payload size in bytes for incoming WebSocket messages. Messages larger than this limit cause the connection to close with MessageTooBig.
requirements: payload is an absolute byte limit; setting 0 will cause any non-empty message to be rejected.
Call before receiving large messages to ensure proper enforcement.

functions.name: crow::websocket::Connection::get_subprotocol
functions.description: Returns the negotiated WebSocket subprotocol string, or an empty string if none was negotiated.
requirements: None.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::dump
functions.description: Formats this cookie (name, value, and any set attributes) into an HTTP Set-Cookie header field-value string. Intended for adding to an HTTP response header via Set-Cookie.
requirements: No explicit preconditions. If no attributes are set, only name and value are emitted.
If value was never set, an empty quoted value ("") is emitted.
Expires uses the fixed HTTP-date format "%a, %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S GMT" via std::put_time; provide a valid std::tm (preferably UTC) via expires() if you need the attribute.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::name
functions.description: Returns the cookie's name (key).
requirements: The cookie must have been constructed (implicitly true); name may be empty if constructed that way.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::value
functions.description: Sets the cookie's value and returns a reference to the cookie to allow chaining. Overwrites any previous value.
requirements: U must be assignable to std::string (e.g., std::string, const char*, std::string_view).
Do not use the returned reference after the Cookie object is destroyed.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::expires
functions.description: Sets the Expires attribute of the cookie using the provided calendar time and returns a reference for chaining. The time is rendered with the HTTP GMT date format when dumped.
requirements: time must reference a valid std::tm structure. No range checks are performed.
Caller is responsible for providing the desired timezone semantics (the formatter prints "GMT" literally).

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::max_age
functions.description: Sets the Max-Age attribute (in seconds) and returns a reference for chaining.
requirements: seconds is stored as-is; no validation is performed (negative values are not rejected by this function).

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::domain
functions.description: Sets the Domain attribute and returns a reference for chaining.
requirements: name is stored verbatim; no validation is performed.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::path
functions.description: Sets the Path attribute and returns a reference for chaining.
requirements: path is stored verbatim; no validation is performed.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::secure
functions.description: Enables the Secure attribute and returns a reference for chaining.
requirements: No parameters; simply flags the cookie as Secure.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::httponly
functions.description: Enables the HttpOnly attribute and returns a reference for chaining.
requirements: No parameters; simply flags the cookie as HttpOnly.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::Cookie::same_site
functions.description: Sets the SameSite attribute to Strict, Lax, or None and returns a reference for chaining.
requirements: ssp must be a valid enumerator of SameSitePolicy (Strict, Lax, or None).

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::context::get_cookie
functions.description: Looks up and returns the value of a parsed request cookie by name. Returns an empty string if not found.
requirements: key is used as-is; lookup is case-sensitive.
Must be called after before_handle has parsed cookies into the context for the current request to have data.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::context::set_cookie
functions.signature: template <typename U> crow::CookieParser::Cookie& crow::CookieParser::context::set_cookie(const std::string& key, U&& value)
functions.description: Creates a new cookie to be added to the response with the given name and value, stores it internally, and returns a reference to allow setting attributes fluently before the response is sent.
requirements: U must be assignable to std::string.

The returned Cookie& refers to an element inside an internal std::vector; references can be invalidated by subsequent insertions/reallocations. Do not keep the reference beyond further modifications that may reallocate or beyond the lifetime of the context.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::before_handle
functions.signature: void crow::CookieParser::before_handle(crow::request& req, crow::response& res, crow::CookieParser::context& ctx)
functions.description: Middleware hook invoked before request handling. Parses the Cookie header into key/value pairs and stores them in ctx.jar. If multiple Cookie headers are present, responds with HTTP 400 and ends the response.
requirements: Call within the middleware pipeline before route handlers that depend on cookies.
Assumes at most one Cookie header; if count > 1, it sets res.code=400 and calls res.end().
Parses cookies by splitting on '=' and ';', trimming spaces, and unquoting simple quoted values.

functions.name: crow::CookieParser::after_handle
functions.description: Middleware hook invoked after request handling. Emits one Set-Cookie header per cookie queued in ctx via set_cookie().
requirements: Call within the middleware pipeline after route handlers.
Expects ctx.cookies_to_add to contain any cookies to set; each is serialized via Cookie::dump() and added with res.add_header("Set-Cookie", ...).

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::origin
functions.description: Sets the Access-Control-Allow-Origin value for this CORS rule. Typical usage: obtain a CORSRules object from CORSHandler (global/prefix/blueprint) and call origin("https://example.com") or origin("*") to configure. Details like value format are not validated by this function.
requirements: Must be called on a CORSRules instance obtained from crow::CORSHandler (cannot be constructed directly).
Passing an empty string results in no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header being set (header is skipped when empty).

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::methods
functions.description: Adds one HTTP method to the Access-Control-Allow-Methods list for this CORS rule. On first non-wildcard call, replaces the default "*" with a comma-separated list. Usage: rules.methods(HTTPMethod::Get).
requirements: Method must be a valid crow::HTTPMethod value.
Must be called on a CORSRules instance obtained from crow::CORSHandler.

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::headers
functions.description: Adds one header name to the Access-Control-Allow-Headers list for this CORS rule. On first non-wildcard call, replaces the default "*" with a comma-separated list.
requirements: Header should be a header field name string; no validation is performed.
Passing an empty string results in no change to outgoing header (empty values are ultimately skipped).
Must be called on a CORSRules instance obtained from crow::CORSHandler.

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::expose
functions.description: Adds one header name to the Access-Control-Expose-Headers list for this CORS rule so that browsers can access it from client code.
requirements: Header should be a header field name string; no validation is performed.
Empty strings are accepted but result in no header being set.
Must be called on a CORSRules instance obtained from crow::CORSHandler.

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::max_age
functions.description: Sets the Access-Control-Max-Age value for this CORS rule by converting the integer to a string. Commonly used to cache preflight results. No range checking is enforced here.
requirements: Must be called on a CORSRules instance obtained from crow::CORSHandler.
If max_age is negative, it will still be converted to a string; behavior is not validated or rejected by this function (caller should ensure appropriate values).

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::allow_credentials
functions.description: Enables Access-Control-Allow-Credentials for this rule. If origin is "*" and the request is not an OPTIONS preflight, the handler will echo the request's Origin header instead of "*" to comply with credentialed requests.
requirements: Must be called on a CORSRules instance obtained from crow::CORSHandler.

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::ignore
functions.description: Disables CORS handling for this rule, causing no CORS headers to be added to responses that match this rule.
requirements: Must be called on a CORSRules instance obtained from crow::CORSHandler.

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::prefix
functions.description: Registers and returns a CORSRules object that applies to requests whose URL path starts with the given prefix. This is a forwarding helper that delegates to the owning CORSHandler.
requirements: Callable only on a CORSRules linked to a CORSHandler (all public instances are).
Prefix matching is simple string prefix; no validation or normalization is performed.

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::blueprint
functions.description: Registers and returns a CORSRules object tied to the provided blueprint's prefix. This forwards to the owning CORSHandler.
requirements: bp must be a valid crow::Blueprint reference.
Callable only on a CORSRules linked to a CORSHandler.

functions.name: crow::CORSRules::global
functions.description: Returns the global CORSRules policy from the owning CORSHandler, allowing configuration of default CORS behavior.
requirements: Callable only on a CORSRules linked to a CORSHandler.

functions.name: crow::CORSHandler::before_handle
functions.signature: void crow::CORSHandler::before_handle(crow::request& req, crow::response& res, crow::CORSHandler::context& ctx)
functions.description: Middleware hook invoked before a request handler. In this implementation it performs no action. Normally called by the Crow framework, not by user code.

req, res, and ctx must be valid objects supplied by the framework.

functions.name: crow::CORSHandler::after_handle
functions.signature: void crow::CORSHandler::after_handle(crow::request& req, crow::response& res, crow::CORSHandler::context& ctx)
functions.description: Middleware hook invoked after a request handler. Applies the matching CORSRules (by URL prefix) to set CORS response headers.
requirements: Intended to be invoked by the Crow middleware pipeline; not meant for manual calls.
req.url should be a valid request path; res must be modifiable.
If matching rules have ignore() set, no CORS headers will be added.

functions.name: crow::CORSHandler::prefix
functions.description: Creates or appends a CORS rule for the given URL path prefix and returns a reference to it for configuration. Rules are stored in insertion order and matched by simple prefix comparison.
requirements: prefix is matched using simple string starts-with semantics; caller should supply the intended leading slash form.
Returned CORSRules reference remains valid as long as the CORSHandler outlives it.

functions.name: crow::CORSHandler::blueprint
functions.description: Creates or appends a CORS rule tied to the given blueprint's prefix, and returns a reference to it for configuration.
requirements: bp must be a valid crow::Blueprint with a meaningful prefix().
Returned CORSRules reference remains valid as long as the CORSHandler outlives it.

functions.name: crow::CORSHandler::global
functions.description: Returns a reference to the global (default) CORSRules used when no prefix-specific rule matches. Configure this to change default CORS behavior.
requirements: Returned CORSRules reference remains valid as long as the CORSHandler instance exists.

functions.name: crow::session::multi_value::json
functions.description: Converts the stored variant value to a Crow JSON write-value (wvalue). Intended for serializing a session value to JSON for persistence or response building.
requirements: The multi_value instance must hold one of the supported types: bool, int64_t, double, or std::string.
Callers should expect allocation when converting strings or numbers to JSON as per crow::json::wvalue semantics.

functions.name: crow::session::multi_value::from_json
functions.description: Creates a multi_value from a Crow JSON read-value (rvalue). Numbers are mapped to double or int64_t (unsigned mapped to int64_t), booleans to bool, and strings to std::string. Other JSON types default to bool(false).
requirements: Input must be a valid crow::json::rvalue.
Only JSON number, boolean, and string types are preserved; other types (arrays/objects/null) result in a stored bool(false).

functions.name: crow::session::multi_value::string
functions.description: Returns the stored value formatted as a string. If the stored type is std::string, that value is returned; otherwise the numeric/bool value is converted via std::to_string.
requirements: For non-string stored types, the textual form follows std::to_string for the underlying type.

functions.name: crow::session::multi_value::get
functions.signature: template <typename T, typename RT = wrap_mv_t<T>> RT crow::session::multi_value::get(const T& fallback)
functions.description: Retrieves the stored value if it matches the requested type RT; otherwise returns the provided fallback. The requested type is derived from T, with integral types (except uint64_t) promoted to int64_t and char* converted to std::string.
requirements: Template parameter T determines the requested return type after wrap rules: integrals (except uint64_t) -> int64_t; char* -> std::string.
If the underlying type does not match RT, the function returns the provided fallback value.
Caller must provide a valid fallback of type T (or convertible to RT).

functions.signature: template <typename T, typename RT = wrap_mv_t<T>> void crow::session::multi_value::set(T val)
functions.description: Sets the stored value, converting the provided value to the internal variant-compatible type using wrap rules (integrals to int64_t except uint64_t, and char* to std::string).
requirements: Template parameter T must be convertible to RT after wrapping rules.
Stores one of: bool, int64_t, double, std::string; other input types must be convertible to these after wrapping.

functions.name: crow::session::ExpirationTracker::add
functions.description: Adds or updates an entry's expiration time. Maintains a set ordered by time for efficient retrieval of the next expiration.
requirements: Key strings should be unique identifiers for tracked entries.
Time is an absolute timestamp in seconds (as used by chrono_time in FileStore).
If the key already exists, its previous record is removed and replaced.

functions.name: crow::session::ExpirationTracker::remove
functions.description: Removes a key from the expiration tracker if present.
requirements: No effect if the key is absent.

functions.name: crow::session::ExpirationTracker::peek_first
functions.description: Returns the soonest expiration timestamp without removing it. If empty, returns std::numeric_limits<uint64_t>::max().
requirements: Callers should interpret max() as 'no expirations scheduled'.

functions.name: crow::session::ExpirationTracker::pop_first
functions.description: Removes and returns the key with the earliest expiration time.
requirements: Must only be called when the tracker is non-empty; otherwise behavior relies on internal assumptions (the implementation does not guard against empty state).
After removal, the internal maps are updated to keep the tracker consistent.

functions.name: crow::session::ExpirationTracker::begin
functions.description: Returns a const iterator to the beginning of the internal ordered set of (time,key) pairs.
requirements: Iterator remains valid as long as the tracker is not modified (standard std::set const_iterator validity rules).

functions.name: crow::session::ExpirationTracker::end
functions.description: Returns a const iterator to the end sentinel of the internal ordered set.
requirements: Use with begin() for iteration; standard iterator validity rules of std::set apply.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::mutex
functions.description: Returns a reference to the session's recursive mutex, creating the session node if necessary. Use to manually synchronize complex multi-step operations on the session.
requirements: If the session node does not exist, it will be created.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::exists
functions.description: Returns whether a session node currently exists for this context.
requirements: No side effects; does not create a session.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::get
functions.signature: template <typename F> auto crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::get(const std::string& key, const F& fallback = F()) -> decltype(std::declval<crow::session::multi_value>().get<F>(std::declval<F>()))
functions.description: Retrieves a value by key from the session, returning the provided fallback if missing or of a different type. The return type is deduced from the fallback using multi_value::get's wrapping rules.
requirements: If no session exists, the fallback is returned.
The fallback type F determines the requested return type (after wrapping rules).

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::set
functions.signature: template <typename T> void crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::set(const std::string& key, T value)
functions.description: Sets or overwrites the value for the given key in the session, marking it dirty for persistence. Creates a session node if needed.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::contains
functions.description: Checks whether the session contains a value for the specified key.
requirements: If no session exists, returns false without creating one.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::apply
functions.signature: template <typename Func> void crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::apply(const std::string& key, const Func& f)

The return type of Func must be storable by multi_value::set (convertible to bool, int64_t, double, or std::string after wrapping).
Operation acquires the session recursive mutex.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::remove
functions.description: Removes the specified key from the session and marks it dirty.
requirements: If no session exists, the call is a no-op.
Operation acquires the session recursive mutex.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::string
functions.description: Returns the value associated with the key formatted as a string, or an empty string if missing or no session exists.
requirements: Operation acquires the session recursive mutex if a session exists.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::keys
functions.description: Returns a vector containing the set of keys currently present in the session. Returns an empty vector if no session exists.
requirements: Operation acquires the session recursive mutex if a session exists.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context::refresh_expiration
functions.description: Requests that the session’s expiration be refreshed on the next save, causing a new cookie with updated expiration to be issued and the store notified.
requirements: No effect if no session exists.
Marks the node for refresh; actual cookie update occurs in SessionMiddleware::after_handle.

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::SessionMiddleware
functions.signature: template <typename... Ts> crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::SessionMiddleware(crow::CookieParser::Cookie cookie, int id_length, Ts... ts)
functions.description: Constructs a SessionMiddleware with a provided cookie prototype, session ID length, and arguments forwarded to the underlying Store constructor.
requirements: cookie is used as a prototype for issuing session cookies.
id_length determines random ID size; should be positive.
Ts... must construct Store via Store(std::forward<Ts>(ts)...).

functions.name: crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::before_handle
functions.signature: template <typename AllContext> void crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::before_handle(crow::request& /*req*/, crow::response& /*res*/, crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context& ctx, AllContext& all_ctx)
functions.description: Loads the session for the incoming request. It reads the session ID from the CookieParser in all_ctx, attaches or loads a cached session node if available and valid, and increments a reference counter.

Store must provide: bool contains(const std::string&), void load(crow::session::CachedSession&).

functions.signature: template <typename AllContext> void crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::after_handle(crow::request& /*req*/, crow::response& /*res*/, crow::SessionMiddleware<Store>::context& ctx, AllContext& all_ctx)

If a new ID is needed, generates a random alphanumeric string of configured length.
Thread safety: serialized with an internal std::mutex.
Exceptions from Store::save are caught and logged.

functions.name: crow::InMemoryStore::load
functions.description: Loads session entries for the given session ID from the in-memory map into the provided session cache node.

functions.name: crow::InMemoryStore::save
functions.description: Persists the session cache node's entries into the in-memory map under its session ID.

functions.name: crow::InMemoryStore::contains
functions.description: Checks whether a session with the given ID exists in the in-memory store.

functions.name: crow::FileStore::FileStore
functions.description: Constructs a file-backed session store rooted at the given folder with the specified expiration window. On construction, reads the expirations index and evicts expired entries.

expiration_seconds defines the TTL for sessions; used when refresh is requested.

functions.name: crow::FileStore::~FileStore
functions.description: Destructor that writes the current expirations index to a .expirations file in the store folder.
requirements: The process must have write permissions to the folder to persist expirations; otherwise file output may fail silently.

functions.name: crow::FileStore::handle_expired
functions.description: Deletes up to three expired session files whose expiration time has passed, to avoid long pauses.
requirements: Relies on expirations_ tracker being populated; should be called before loading to keep the store clean.

functions.name: crow::FileStore::load
functions.description: Loads session key-value entries from the JSON file corresponding to cn.session_id, after handling a limited number of expirations.

functions.name: crow::FileStore::get_filename

functions.description: Builds the absolute filename for a given session key under the store path, optionally adding the .json suffix.
requirements: key is the session identifier or a special key (e.g., ".expirations").
If suffix is true, ".json" is appended.

functions.name: crow::FileStore::contains
functions.description: Checks whether the JSON file for the given session key exists and is readable.
requirements: Relies on filesystem access; returns false if the file cannot be opened.

functions.name: crow::FileStore::evict
functions.description: Removes the session file for the given key from disk.

functions.description: Feeds a single byte into the hash computation. Buffers bytes and processes 64-byte blocks as needed.
requirements: May be called repeatedly to stream input data

functions.name: sha1::SHA1::processBlock
functions.signature: SHA1& processBlock(const void* const start, const void* const end)
functions.description: Feeds a contiguous range of bytes [start, end) into the hash, forwarding each byte to processByte. Convenient for processing an existing memory range.
requirements: start and end must denote a valid contiguous byte range in the same allocated object/array
start must be less than or equal to end; if start > end the loop would never terminate
The memory in [start, end) must be readable for the entire range
Must not be called after finalization via getDigest/getDigestBytes unless reset() is called first

functions.name: sha1::SHA1::processBytes
functions.signature: SHA1& processBytes(const void* const data, size_t len)
functions.description: Feeds len bytes from data into the hash computation by delegating to processBlock over the range [data, data + len).
requirements: If len > 0, data must be a valid non-null pointer to at least len readable bytes

Must not be called after finalization via getDigest/getDigestBytes unless reset() is called first

functions.name: sha1::SHA1::getDigest
functions.description: Finalizes the hash by padding the message and appending the length, then writes the 160-bit SHA-1 result as five big-endian 32-bit words into digest. Returns digest.
requirements: digest must point to storage for 5 uint32_t elements
Must be called only after all input has been provided via processByte/processBytes
Calling this function modifies and finalizes the internal state (pads the message); do not continue feeding data afterward unless you call reset()
The implementation encodes only the lower 32 bits of the bit length (high 32 bits set to zero); for correct results, total message length must be less than 2^32 bits (i.e., < 512 MiB)
May be called at most once per message; repeated calls without reset() will produce incorrect results

functions.name: sha1::SHA1::getDigestBytes

requirements: digest must point to storage for 20 uint8_t elements
Must be called only after all input has been provided via processByte/processBytes
Calling this function finalizes the internal state; do not continue feeding data afterward unless you call reset()
Subject to the same message-length limitation as getDigest: total length must be < 2^32 bits (~512 MiB)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: HTTP header value
# Guidance: arbitrary string used as value portion; visible characters; no validation required.
# Goal: produce interesting yet valid header values that can exercise library code paths
# in Crow involving headers (case-insensitive map, presence/absence, lengths, commas, etc.).

VISIBLE = ''.join(chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7f) if chr(c) not in '\r\n')
# Common tokens that appear in header values
TOKENS = [
    "text/plain", "text/html; charset=utf-8", "application/json", "gzip", "br", "deflate",
    "no-cache", "max-age=0", "keep-alive", "close", "chunked", "bytes", "attachment",
    "filename=example.txt", "boundary=CROW-BOUNDARY", "Bearer abcdef123456", "Basic QWxhZGRpbjpvcGVuIHNlc2FtZQ==",
    "en-US,en;q=0.9", "*/*", "private", "public", "immutable", "s-maxage=86400",
]

# Generators for structured values

def rand_token(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    return rnd.choice(TOKENS)

def rand_quoted(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # generate a quoted-string with escapable characters per RFC-ish style
    length = rnd.randint(0, 32)
    chars = []
    for _ in range(length):
        ch = rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:+@$")
        if ch in '\\"':
            chars.append('\\' + ch)
        else:
            chars.append(ch)
    return '"' + ''.join(chars) + '"'

def rand_params(rnd: random.Random, kmin=1, kmax=4) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(kmin, kmax)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(n):
        key_len = rnd.randint(1, 8)
        key = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + '-') for _ in range(key_len))
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            val = rand_quoted(rnd)
        else:
            val_len = rnd.randint(1, 10)
            val = ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '-._') for _ in range(val_len))
        parts.append(f"{key}={val}")
    return '; '.join(parts)

def rand_csv(rnd: random.Random, item_gen, count_min=2, count_max=6) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(count_min, count_max)
    items = [item_gen(rnd) for _ in range(n)]
    # include quality weights occasionally
    if rnd.random() < 0.5:
        with_q = []
        for it in items:
            if rnd.random() < 0.5:
                q = rnd.uniform(0, 1)
                with_q.append(f"{it}; q={q:.1f}")
            else:
                with_q.append(it)
        items = with_q
    return ', '.join(items)

def rand_visible(rnd: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=128) -> str:
    n = rnd.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rnd.choice(VISIBLE) for _ in range(n))

# Catalog of interesting header value patterns

def build_candidates(rnd: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    c = []
    # Empty and simple
    c.append("")
    c.append(" ")
    c.append("0")
    c.append("true")
    c.append("false")
    c.append("UTF-8")
    # MIME types
    c.append("application/octet-stream")
    c.append("text/plain; charset=UTF-8")
    c.append("multipart/form-data; boundary=CROW-BOUNDARY")
    # Caching
    c.append("no-cache")
    c.append("max-age=3600, public")
    # Encodings
    c.append("gzip, deflate, br")
    # Ranges
    c.append("bytes=0-1023")
    c.append("bytes=0-")
    # Disposition
    c.append("attachment; filename=\"report.pdf\"")
    # Authorization
    c.append("Bearer " + ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(24)))
    c.append("Basic " + ''.join(rnd.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '+/=') for _ in range(28)))
    # Dates (RFC1123 style)
    c.append("Sun, 06 Nov 1994 08:49:37 GMT")
    # ETag
    c.append('W/"xyzzy"')
    c.append('"abcdef123456"')
    # CSV lists
    c.append(rand_csv(rnd, lambda r: r.choice(["en-US", "en", "fr", "de", "es", "*"])))
    c.append(rand_csv(rnd, lambda r: r.choice(["text/html", "application/json", "image/png", "*/*"])))
    # Parameters
    c.append("token; " + rand_params(rnd))
    c.append(rand_token(rnd) + "; " + rand_params(rnd))
    # Quoted strings
    c.append(rand_quoted(rnd))
    # Large but bounded value (to test Content-Length-like or general storage)
    c.append(rand_visible(rnd, 64, 256))
    # Cookie-like value content
    c.append("session=abcdef123456; Path=/; HttpOnly")
    # CORS-like values
    c.append("*")
    c.append("https://example.com")
    # Random visible
    c.append(rand_visible(rnd, 1, 64))
    return c


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    candidates = build_candidates(rnd)
    # Mix with a few additional randomized structures for diversity per call
    choice_pool = candidates + [
        rand_csv(rnd, lambda r: rand_token(r)),
        rand_token(rnd),
        rand_token(rnd) + "; " + rand_params(rnd),
        rand_visible(rnd, 0, 128),
    ]
    value = rnd.choice(choice_pool)
    # Ensure total length within limit
    if len(value) > 4096:
        value = value[:4096]
    return value.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target: Produce interesting valid arbitrary strings to feed many Crow components.
# Strategy: Generate a mix of:
# - ASCII printable strings
# - Path-like and filename-like strings
# - HTTP header-like lines
# - JSON snippets (valid)
# - URL query strings with lists and dicts
# - Multipart boundaries and bodies
# - Cookie headers and Set-Cookie fragments
# - Base64-like random bytes
# - WebSocket control-sized payloads
# The buffer is a single bytes blob. The harness will slice and use as needed.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

RAND = random.Random()

ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PRINTABLE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-./:@?&=%,+;[]{}()<>\"'\\\n\r\t"


def _rand_ascii(n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(RAND.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_printable(n: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(RAND.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(n))


def _json_valid() -> str:
    # Produce a small valid JSON snippet of varying shapes
    choice = RAND.randrange(6)
    if choice == 0:
        return "{}"
    if choice == 1:
        return "[]"
    if choice == 2:
        return f'"{_rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0,40))}"'
    if choice == 3:
        # small object
        k1 = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(1,6))
        k2 = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(1,6))
        v1 = RAND.randrange(0, 1000)
        v2 = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0,20))
        return f'{{"{k1}": {v1}, "{k2}": "{v2}"}}'
    if choice == 4:
        # array
        elems = [str(RAND.randrange(0,100)) for _ in range(RAND.randrange(1,6))]
        return '[' + ','.join(elems) + ']'
    # boolean/null
    return RAND.choice(["true","false","null"])


def _query_string() -> str:
    # Includes list and dict styles
    base = []
    # simple pairs
    for _ in range(RAND.randrange(1,4)):
        k = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(1,6))
        v = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0,10))
        base.append(f"{k}={v}")
    # list form name[]=v
    name = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(3,7))
    for _ in range(RAND.randrange(1,3)):
        base.append(f"{name}[]={_rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(0,6))}")
    # dict form dict[key]=v
    dname = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(3,7))
    for sub in ["a","b"]:
        base.append(f"{dname}[{sub}]={_rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(0,6))}")
    return '&'.join(base)


def _cookie_header() -> str:
    # Cookie: k1=v1; k2="v2"; k3=v3
    parts = []
    for _ in range(RAND.randrange(1,4)):
        k = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(1,8))
        v = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0,10))
        if RAND.randrange(2):
            parts.append(f"{k}={v}")
        else:
            parts.append(f"{k}=\"{v}\"")
    return '; '.join(parts)


def _set_cookie() -> str:
    k = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(1,8))
    v = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0,12))
    attrs: List[str] = []
    if RAND.randrange(2):
        attrs.append(f"Domain={_rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(3,10)).lower()}.example")
    if RAND.randrange(2):
        attrs.append(f"Path=/{_rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(0,5))}")
    if RAND.randrange(2):
        attrs.append("Secure")
    if RAND.randrange(2):
        attrs.append("HttpOnly")
    if RAND.randrange(2):
        attrs.append("SameSite=" + RAND.choice(["Strict","Lax","None"]))
    return f"{k}={v}; " + '; '.join(attrs) if attrs else f"{k}={v}"


def _multipart(boundary: str) -> str:
    # Minimal multipart body with 1-2 parts, CRLF line endings
    parts = []
    n = RAND.randrange(1,3)
    for i in range(n):
        name = f"field{i}"
        body = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0,40))
        headers = [
            f"Content-Disposition: form-data; name=\"{name}\"",
        ]
        if RAND.randrange(2):
            headers.append("Content-Type: text/plain")
        section = "--" + boundary + "\r\n" + "\r\n".join(headers) + "\r\n\r\n" + body + "\r\n"
        parts.append(section)
    closing = "--" + boundary + "--\r\n"
    return ''.join(parts) + closing


def _header_lines() -> str:
    # Some varied header lines (ci_map usage)
    keys = ["Content-Type","X-Test","Accept","Server","Set-Cookie"]
    lines = []
    for _ in range(RAND.randrange(2,5)):
        k = RAND.choice(keys)
        if k == "Set-Cookie":
            v = _set_cookie()
        elif k == "Content-Type":
            v = RAND.choice([
                "text/plain", "text/html", "application/json",
                "multipart/form-data; boundary=" + _rand_ascii(10)
            ])
        else:
            v = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0,20))
        lines.append(f"{k}: {v}")
    return "\r\n".join(lines)


def _path_like() -> str:
    segs = [ _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(1,6)) for _ in range(RAND.randrange(1,4)) ]
    return "/" + "/".join(segs)


def _mustache() -> str:
    # Simple valid mustache template with tags
    name = _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(3,8))
    tmpl = "Hello {{" + name + "}}!\n" + "{{#list}}- {{.}}\n{{/list}}\n"
    return tmpl


def _base64_bytes(n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(RAND.randrange(0,256) for _ in range(n))


def _join_sections(sections: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    out = b"\n---\n".join(sections)
    if len(out) > MAX_TOTAL:
        out = out[:MAX_TOTAL]
    return out


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    RAND.seed(seed)

    sections: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) JSON snippets
    for _ in range(3):
        sections.append(_json_valid().encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 2) URL query strings and full URLs
    qs = _query_string()
    url = f"{_path_like()}?{qs}"
    sections.append(url.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 3) HTTP-like headers
    sections.append(_header_lines().encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 4) Cookie header and Set-Cookie
    sections.append(("Cookie: " + _cookie_header()).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    sections.append(("Set-Cookie: " + _set_cookie()).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 5) Multipart body with boundary
    boundary = "CROW-" + _rand_ascii(12)
    sections.append(("boundary=" + boundary).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    sections.append(_multipart(boundary).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 6) Mustache template content
    sections.append(_mustache().encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 7) Filenames and directories
    fname = _rand_ascii(6) + ".txt"
    d1 = "/tmp/" + _rand_ascii(5)
    d2 = "."  # safe current dir
    sections.append(fname.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    sections.append(d1.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    sections.append(d2.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 8) WebSocket control payload (<=125 bytes)
    ws_payload = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(0, 120))
    sections.append(ws_payload.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 9) Random printable and ASCII blocks
    sections.append(_rand_printable(RAND.randrange(20, 80)).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    sections.append(_rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(10, 40)).encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 10) Base64 source bytes (binary)
    sections.append(_base64_bytes(RAND.randrange(8, 64)))

    # 11) MIME types
    mime_parent = RAND.choice([
        "application/","audio/","font/","example/","image/","message/",
        "model/","multipart/","text/","video/"
    ])
    mime = mime_parent + _rand_ascii(RAND.randrange(3,10))
    sections.append(mime.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    # 12) Case-variation strings to exercise ci_hash/ci_key_eq
    base = _rand_printable(RAND.randrange(5, 40))
    variant = ''.join(ch.swapcase() if ch.isalpha() else ch for ch in base)
    sections.append(base.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
    sections.append(variant.encode('utf-8', 'ignore'))

    return _join_sections(sections)

import string
from typing import List

# Data type: HTTP header name
# Goal: generate interesting, valid HTTP header field-names to exercise Crow's ci_map lookups
# Constraints: field-name is token per RFC 7230: one or more tchar characters
# tchar = !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~ or DIGIT or ALPHA. No spaces, no colon.
# Crow treats keys case-insensitively, so vary case patterns and include common standard/custom names.

TCHARS = "!#$%&'*+-.^_`|~" + string.ascii_letters + string.digits

COMMON_HEADERS = [
    # Standard/common headers
    "Content-Type", "Content-Length", "Content-Encoding", "Content-Language",
    "Content-Location", "Content-Disposition", "Content-Range",
    "Accept", "Accept-Encoding", "Accept-Language", "Accept-Charset",
    "User-Agent", "Host", "Authorization", "Proxy-Authorization",
    "Cache-Control", "Pragma", "Expires", "Date", "ETag",
    "If-Modified-Since", "If-None-Match", "If-Match", "If-Unmodified-Since",
    "Location", "Range", "Referer", "Origin", "Cookie", "Set-Cookie",
    "Upgrade", "Connection", "Transfer-Encoding", "TE",
    "X-Requested-With", "X-Forwarded-For", "X-Forwarded-Proto", "X-Real-IP",
    # Websocket related
    "Sec-WebSocket-Key", "Sec-WebSocket-Accept", "Sec-WebSocket-Protocol",
    "Sec-WebSocket-Version",
    # Custom prefixes
    "X-Test", "X-Fuzz-Header", "X-Custom-Token", "X-Trace-Id",
]

CASE_FUNCS = [
    str.lower,
    str.upper,
    lambda s: s,  # original/mixed
    lambda s: ''.join(c.lower() if i % 2 else c.upper() for i, c in enumerate(s)),
]

def rand_token(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 40) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(TCHARS) for _ in range(n))

def rand_header_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Weighted choice among: common header (with case variation), X- prefix custom, random token, hyphenated tokens
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.4:
        base = rng.choice(COMMON_HEADERS)
        casef = rng.choice(CASE_FUNCS)
        return casef(base)
    elif choice < 0.7:
        # X- prefix with token parts
        parts = ["X", rand_token(rng, 3, 10)]
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(rand_token(rng, 2, 8))
        return '-'.join(parts)
    else:
        # Hyphenated random tokens (2-4 parts)
        k = rng.randint(1, 3)
        parts = [rand_token(rng, 2, rng.randint(4, 12)) for _ in range(k + 1)]
        return '-'.join(parts)

def build_corpus(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    corpus: List[str] = []
    # Seed with a deterministic diverse set
    corpus.extend(COMMON_HEADERS[:])
    # Case-variant duplicates for some keys to exercise ci_map equality
    for base in ["Content-Type", "X-Fuzz-Header", "Cookie"]:
        corpus.append(base.lower())
        corpus.append(base.upper())
        corpus.append(''.join(c.lower() if i % 2 else c.upper() for i, c in enumerate(base)))
    # Some random customs
    for _ in range(16):
        corpus.append(rand_header_name(rng))
    # Ensure unique while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq = []
    for h in corpus:
        if h not in seen:
            seen.add(h)
            uniq.append(h)
    return uniq

def pick_interesting_pair(rng: random.Random, headers: List[str]) -> bytes:
    # For these fuzzers, FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used for keys and sometimes also for values.
    # We return a single header name per invocation; the harness will use it in different roles.
    # To make a single buffer provide multiple options, we serialize multiple header names separated by newlines.
    # The runtime may split or consume as needed; at minimum, the first line will be a valid header name.
    count = rng.randint(3, min(20, len(headers)))
    chosen = rng.sample(headers, count)
    # Also include specifically crafted collision-like cases (differ only by case)
    key = rng.choice(COMMON_HEADERS)
    chosen.extend([key, key.lower(), key.upper()])
    # Limit total size <= 4096
    payload = '\n'.join(chosen)
    b = payload.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        b = b[:4096]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    headers = build_corpus(rng)
    return pick_interesting_pair(rng, headers)

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for application/x-www-form-urlencoded payloads and related query-ish inputs
# Target fuzzers exercise Crow's qs_* routines and request::get_body_params().
# We produce well-formed, interesting URL-encoded key/value sequences with variants
# (lists using [], dict-style name[sub]=val, mixed encodings, reserved chars, unicode, long/short values, etc.).

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.*"
RESERVED = ":/?#[]@!$&'()*+,;="
HEX = "0123456789ABCDEF"


def _percent_encode_byte(b: int) -> str:
    return "%" + HEX[(b >> 4) & 0xF] + HEX[b & 0xF]


def _percent_encode(s: str, plus_for_space: bool = True) -> str:
    out = []
    for ch in s:
        o = ord(ch)
        if ch == " " and plus_for_space:
            out.append("+")
        elif ch in SAFE_CHARS:
            out.append(ch)
        elif o < 0x80:
            out.append(_percent_encode_byte(o))
        else:
            # UTF-8 percent-encode
            for b in ch.encode("utf-8"):
                out.append(_percent_encode_byte(b))
    return "".join(out)


def _rand_word(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=10, allow_reserved=False) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII, digits, some unicode
    pool = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
    if allow_reserved:
        pool += RESERVED
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = "".join(rng.choice(pool) for _ in range(length))
    # Occasionally inject unicode
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        uni_samples = [" café", "東京", "✓", "💡", "ñ", "ł", "€", "Ω"]
        s = s + rng.choice(uni_samples)
    return s


def _kv_pair(rng: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    # Choose different key styles to hit qs_k2v, get_list, get_dict
    style = rng.randint(0, 4)
    base = _rand_word(rng, 1, 8, allow_reserved=False)
    if style == 0:
        key = base
    elif style == 1:
        key = base + "[]"  # list style
    elif style == 2:
        key = f"{base}[{_rand_word(rng,1,5)}]"  # dict style
    elif style == 3:
        key = base + rng.choice(["-id", "_id", ".x"])  # dotted/suffixed
    else:
        # include reserved characters to test decoding path; then percent-encode later
        key = base + rng.choice([":scope", "@hdr", "/path"])
    # Value variety
    v_style = rng.randint(0, 6)
    if v_style == 0:
        val = str(rng.randint(-10_000, 10_000))
    elif v_style == 1:
        val = str(rng.random() * (1000 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 1))
    elif v_style == 2:
        val = _rand_word(rng, 0, 16, allow_reserved=True)
    elif v_style == 3:
        # long value
        val = _rand_word(rng, 32, 96, allow_reserved=True)
    elif v_style == 4:
        # Already-encoded sequences, including spaces as + and mixed percent
        raw = "value with spaces & symbols/"
        val = raw.replace(" ", "+") + "%2Fend"  # contains %
    elif v_style == 5:
        # UTF-8 heavy
        val = rng.choice(["mañana", "crème brûlée", "Привет", "数据", "😀emoji"])
    else:
        # Empty
        val = ""
    return key, val


def _build_form(rng: random.Random, target_size: int) -> str:
    # Assemble query/body. Sometimes include a full URL prefix to exercise parse_url true.
    parts: List[str] = []
    count = rng.randint(3, 20)
    for _ in range(count):
        k, v = _kv_pair(rng)
        # Randomly choose to encode key/value differently to exercise decoder paths
        enc_key = _percent_encode(k, plus_for_space=True) if rng.random() < 0.8 else k
        enc_val = _percent_encode(v, plus_for_space=True) if rng.random() < 0.8 else v
        parts.append(f"{enc_key}={enc_val}")
        # Occasionally add bare keys (no '=') or empty params
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            parts.append(_percent_encode(_rand_word(rng,1,6), plus_for_space=True))
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            parts.append("")
    body = "&".join(parts)

    # Inject anchors and fragments occasionally and extra separators
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        body += "#fragment" + _percent_encode(_rand_word(rng,3,6))
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        body = body.replace("&", "&&", 1)

    # Sometimes prepend a URL to exercise qs_parse(url=true)
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        scheme = rng.choice(["http", "https"])
        host = _rand_word(rng, 3, 6) + ".example.com"
        path = "/" + _percent_encode(_rand_word(rng, 1, 6))
        prefix = f"{scheme}://{host}{path}?"
        body = prefix + body

    # Trim to target_size softly, ensuring not to cut inside percent triplet mid-sequence
    if len(body) > target_size:
        cut = target_size
        # back up to avoid cutting a %HH
        if cut > 0 and body[cut-1] == '%':
            cut -= 1
        elif cut > 1 and body[cut-2] == '%':
            cut -= 2
        body = body[:max(0, cut)]
    return body


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose a target overall size up to 1024 to align with fuzzers' caps
    target_size = rng.randint(64, 768)
    form = _build_form(rng, target_size)

    # Occasionally tailor toward dict/list lookups to boost positive paths in qs_dict_name2kv/qs_k2v
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = _rand_word(rng, 3, 6, allow_reserved=False)
        # Ensure presence
        extras = [
            f"{base}%5Ba%5D=1",  # base[a]=1 (percent-encoded brackets)
            f"{base}[b]=2",
            f"{base}[]=x",
            f"{base}[]=y"
        ]
        joiner = '&' if ('?' not in form) else '&'
        form = (form + joiner + '&'.join(extras))[:min(len(form) + 256, 1024)]

    # Ensure non-empty and NUL-safe; the fuzzer uses std::string, no need to add trailing NUL
    if not form:
        form = "a=1&b=2"

    # Cap absolute maximum per instruction
    if len(form) > 4096:
        form = form[:4096]

    return form.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets three fuzz stubs that consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# We will encode a small container format that the fuzz harness can read via its parameter API
# such that:
#  - FUZZ_PARAM_STR returns interesting MIME-like strings and content types
#  - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME points to a plausible existing regular file path name (we provide names)
# The data is valid, not malformed, aiming to exercise:
#   - crow::response::validate_mime_type with valid parent/subtype pairs
#   - crow::response::set_static_file_info with filenames likely to exist (e.g., /etc/hosts) or not
#   - crow::UTF8::after_handle with reasonable content-type values
#
# Encoding format (simple length-prefixed records):
#   [count (1 byte)] then for each record:
#       [kind (1 byte): 0 = filename, 1 = string]
#       [len (2 bytes LE)]
#       [payload bytes]
# The total stays well under 4096 bytes.

TOP_LEVEL_TYPES = [
    "application/", "audio/", "font/", "example/", "image/", "message/",
    "model/", "multipart/", "text/", "video/",
]

# Some common existing files for typical Linux containers and macOS; these are harmless reads.
COMMON_FILES = [
    "/etc/hosts",
    "/etc/services",
    "/etc/protocols",
    "/etc/resolv.conf",
    "/etc/passwd",  # may exist; only stat is performed by Crow
]

# Some certainly-nonexistent paths to drive the 404 branch.
FAKE_FILES = [
    "/tmp/crow_no_such_file_{}.dat",
    "/var/tmp/crow_missing_{}.bin",
]

# A set of reasonable extensions to trigger auto Content-Type mapping path in set_static_file_info
EXTENSIONS = [
    "txt", "html", "json", "xml", "png", "jpg", "jpeg", "gif", "css", "js", "pdf", "bin",
]

# Reasonable explicit content types for testing both valid and edge cases (non-empty strings)
EXPLICIT_CT = [
    "text/plain", "text/html", "application/json", "application/octet-stream",
    "image/png", "image/jpeg", "multipart/form-data", "audio/mpeg", "video/mp4",
]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Use URL-safe and header-friendly characters
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.+"
    return "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))


def _make_valid_mime(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    parent = rng.choice(TOP_LEVEL_TYPES)
    # Ensure non-empty subtype
    subtype_core = _rand_ascii(rng, 3, 16)
    # Optionally add structured syntax suffix or tree (e.g., vnd., +json)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        subtype_core = "vnd." + subtype_core
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        subtype_core = subtype_core + "+json"
    return parent + subtype_core


def _choose_filename_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []
    # Include some real files that likely exist
    for path in COMMON_FILES:
        out.append(path)
    # Add some temp files with extensions to exercise mime-from-extension branch
    tmp_dir = "/tmp"
    base = f"crow_seed_{rng.randint(0, 1_000_000)}"
    for i in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        ext = rng.choice(EXTENSIONS)
        out.append(os.path.join(tmp_dir, f"{base}_{i}.{ext}"))  # likely non-existent but well-formed
    # Add guaranteed-missing patterns
    for patt in FAKE_FILES:
        out.append(patt.format(rng.randint(1000, 9999)))
    return out


def _pack_record(kind: int, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
    # kind: 0 filename, 1 string
    if len(payload) > 0xFFFF:
        payload = payload[:0xFFFF]
    return bytes([kind]) + len(payload).to_bytes(2, "little") + payload


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    records: List[bytes] = []

    # 1) Provide a handful of valid MIME types for validate_mime_type and for explicit content types
    for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 5)):
        ct = _make_valid_mime(rng)
        records.append(_pack_record(1, ct.encode("ascii", "ignore")))

    # 2) Also include some non-empty arbitrary strings to feed other FUZZ_PARAM_STR uses
    for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        s = _rand_ascii(rng, 4, 24)
        records.append(_pack_record(1, s.encode("ascii", "ignore")))

    # 3) Include known good explicit content-types
    for ct in rng.sample(EXPLICIT_CT, k=rng.randint(2, min(4, len(EXPLICIT_CT)))):
        records.append(_pack_record(1, ct.encode("ascii")))

    # 4) Filenames: mix of common existing and synthetic paths
    for path in _choose_filename_set(rng):
        records.append(_pack_record(0, path.encode("utf-8")))

    # 5) Add some filenames with reasonable names in current directory (no IO performed here)
    for i in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
        nm = f"file_{_rand_ascii(rng, 5, 12)}.{rng.choice(EXTENSIONS)}"
        records.append(_pack_record(0, nm.encode("utf-8")))

    # Assemble buffer: count + records
    # Cap total size to 4096 bytes
    out = bytearray()
    # Placeholder for count
    out.append(0)
    count = 0
    for rec in records:
        if 1 + len(out) + len(rec) > 4096:
            break
        out.extend(rec)
        count += 1
    out[0] = count & 0xFF
    return bytes(out)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: MIME type or extension string
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() once to build a subtype for a full MIME type like "text/<subtype>".
# It also tests mapping from a common extension (hardcoded to html) and an invalid string internally.
# Our goal is to provide an initial interesting buffer that FUZZ_PARAM_STR() will read from.
# Many fuzzing frameworks treat the provided bytes as a pool consumed sequentially by FUZZ_PARAM_* calls.
# We'll therefore encode one or more candidate strings separated by newlines. The first will be used.
# We keep inputs valid and diverse: common subtypes, uncommon but valid, edge lengths (1..8), and characters.

_VALID_SUBTYPES = [
    "plain", "html", "css", "csv", "javascript", "xml", "json", "markdown",
    "event-stream", "calendar", "rtf", "x-python", "x-c++hdr", "x-csrc",
    "x-msdownload", "x-sh", "x-bat", "vcard", "uri-list", "x-yaml",
]

# Generate a random valid token for MIME subtype per RFC-ish token: letters, digits, and -.+
_TOKEN_CHARS = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-+."


def _rand_subtype(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # length 1..8 per stub clamp; ensure non-empty
    n = rng.randint(1, 8)
    s = ''.join(rng.choice(_TOKEN_CHARS) for _ in range(n))
    # Avoid starting with '.' which could be odd; start with alnum if possible
    if s[0] in ".+":
        s = rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) + s[1:]
    return s


def _interesting_subtypes(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    subs = []
    # Hand-picked common/edge values
    subs.extend([
        "plain",           # typical
        "html",            # typical
        "json",            # typical
        "csv",             # short
        "x",               # minimal non-empty
        "x-json",          # vendor style
        "x.y-z+v9",        # complex token within allowed set
        "markdown",        # longer than clamp
        "event-stream",    # hyphen
    ])
    # Random additional values
    for _ in range(5):
        subs.append(_rand_subtype(rng))
    # Shuffle for variability
    rng.shuffle(subs)
    return subs


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Build multiple candidate lines; FUZZ_PARAM_STR() likely reads one string
    candidates = _interesting_subtypes(rng)
    # Ensure first is within 1..8 characters after stub clamp; if not, move a short one to front
    def fits(s: str) -> bool:
        return 1 <= len(s) <= 8
    short_idx = next((i for i, s in enumerate(candidates) if fits(s)), None)
    if short_idx is not None and short_idx != 0:
        candidates[0], candidates[short_idx] = candidates[short_idx], candidates[0]

    # Join with newlines so additional FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads (if any) see more values.
    payload = "\n".join(candidates)
    # Limit total size
    data = payload.encode("utf-8")[:4096]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: URL or path string
# We will generate a single buffer that the harness will split into multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
# Common pattern: concatenate several NUL-terminated strings.
# The stubs request up to 4 strings (redirect, redirect_perm, moved, moved_perm) and utility functions
# may request additional strings (join_path uses two). We will provide a sequence of 8 strings.
# Each string is crafted to be a valid and interesting URL/path: absolute URLs, relative paths,
# paths with dot segments, query/fragment, Unicode, percent-encoding, and edge slashes.

_SCHEMES = [
    "http", "https", "ftp", "ws", "wss"
]

_HOSTS = [
    "example.com", "xn--exmple-cua.com", "localhost", "127.0.0.1", "[::1]",
    "sub.domain.example", "例え.テスト"
]

_PATH_PARTS = [
    "", "a", "b", "c", "..", ".", "%2E", "%2e", "d", "e", "static", "api", "v1",
]

_QUERY_KEYS = ["q", "id", "page", "redirect", "lang", "empty", "arr[]", "dict[key]"]
_QUERY_VALS = ["", "1", "42", "../x", "a/b", "c%2Fd", "ümlaut", "中文", "true", "false"]

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, arr: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(arr)

def _rand_int(rng: random.Random, a: int, b: int) -> int:
    return rng.randint(a, b)

def _rand_host(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    host = _rand_choice(rng, _HOSTS)
    # Optionally add port
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        port = _rand_int(rng, 1, 65535)
        host = f"{host}:{port}"
    return host

def _rand_path(rng: random.Random, allow_empty_start: bool = False) -> str:
    # Build a path with random segments, preserving validity
    segs = []
    n = _rand_int(rng, 0, 5)
    for _ in range(n):
        segs.append(_rand_choice(rng, _PATH_PARTS))
    path = "/".join(segs)
    if not allow_empty_start:
        if not path.startswith("/"):
            path = "/" + path
    # Optionally add trailing slash
    if rng.random() < 0.7 and not path.endswith("/"):
        path += "/"
    return path

def _rand_query(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        return ""
    params = []
    m = _rand_int(rng, 1, 4)
    for _ in range(m):
        k = _rand_choice(rng, _QUERY_KEYS)
        v = _rand_choice(rng, _QUERY_VALS)
        params.append(f"{k}={v}")
    return "?" + "&".join(params)

def _rand_fragment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return ""
    frag = rng.choice(["top", "section-1", "äöü", "%F0%9F%9A%80", ""])  # allow empty after '#'
    return "#" + frag

def _absolute_url(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    scheme = _rand_choice(rng, _SCHEMES)
    host = _rand_host(rng)
    path = _rand_path(rng)
    q = _rand_query(rng)
    f = _rand_fragment(rng)
    return f"{scheme}://{host}{path}{q}{f}"

def _relative_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Application-relative
    base = _rand_path(rng)
    q = _rand_query(rng)
    f = _rand_fragment(rng)
    return f"{base}{q}{f}"

def _path_edge_cases(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    return [
        "/",  # root
        "//",  # double slash
        "/./a/b/../c/",  # dot segments
        "/%2E/%2e/..//a",  # encoded dot segments and double slash
        "/a b/c d/",  # spaces
        "/a%20b/c%2Fd/",  # percent-encoded
        "/a" * _rand_int(rng, 1, 10) + "/",  # long repetitive
    ]

def _random_leaf(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # For join_path leaf parts; may or may not start with slash
    leaf = rng.choice([
        "file.txt", "./file", "../up", "", "nested/leaf", "/abs/leaf",
        "üñïçødé", "data.json", "index.html", "..", "."
    ])
    return leaf

def _random_base(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    base = rng.choice([
        "/base", "/base/", "", "/", "//netloc/style/", "/api/v1",
        "C:/windows/path" if rng.random() < 0.3 else "/posix/path"
    ])
    return base

def _gen_strings(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    out: List[str] = []
    # 1-4: absolute URLs and relative paths for redirect-like functions
    out.append(_absolute_url(rng))
    out.append(_relative_path(rng))
    out.append(_absolute_url(rng))
    out.append(_relative_path(rng))
    # 5-6: inputs for join_path
    out.append(_random_base(rng))
    out.append(_random_leaf(rng))
    # 7-8: edge-case paths for normalize_path and more join_path
    edges = _path_edge_cases(rng)
    out.append(rng.choice(edges))
    out.append(rng.choice(edges))
    # Ensure size constraints per stub (they cap at 256/128). We'll just cap to 240 to be safe.
    out = [s[:240] for s in out]
    # Ensure Location header values non-empty
    out = [s if s else "/" for s in out]
    return out

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    strings = _gen_strings(rng)
    # Compose as NUL-terminated sequence; FUZZ harness typically pulls sequentially.
    # Add an extra final empty string to avoid out-of-data reads.
    payload = bytearray()
    for s in strings:
        payload.extend(s.encode('utf-8', 'strict'))
        payload.append(0)
    payload.extend(b"\x00")
    # Limit total size
    return bytes(payload[:4096])

import random
import base64
from typing import List

# We generate a raw byte payload, then encode it using either standard or URL-safe
# base64, optionally with/without padding, and sometimes insert newlines to
# exercise decoders that tolerate/ignore whitespace. The fuzzer stub will take
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR, encode itself again and then decode; providing already-base64
# text with varied alphabets and padding ensures encode/decode paths are all valid
# and round-trip comparisons remain meaningful.

ALPH_STD = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"
ALPH_URL = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_"


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _maybe_strip_padding(rng: random.Random, b64: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Randomly strip '=' padding (valid for many decoders when length implies padding)
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        return b64.rstrip(b"=")
    return b64


def _maybe_add_newlines(rng: random.Random, b64: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Insert newlines every 76 chars or at random positions (still valid base64 for many decoders)
    if not b64:
        return b64
    mode = rng.choice(["none", "fixed76", "random"])
    if mode == "none":
        return b64
    if mode == "fixed76":
        chunks = [b64[i:i+76] for i in range(0, len(b64), 76)]
        return b"\n".join(chunks)
    # random insertion
    pieces: List[bytes] = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(b64):
        step = rng.randint(20, 120)
        pieces.append(b64[i:i+step])
        i += step
    return b"\r\n".join(pieces)


def _encode_payload(rng: random.Random, raw: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Choose alphabet and padding/layout variants
    use_url = rng.random() < 0.5
    if use_url:
        b64 = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw)
    else:
        b64 = base64.b64encode(raw)
    # Maybe convert between alphabets by mapping characters (keeps validity)
    # This allows us to produce URL-safe or standard regardless of chosen encoder
    target_url = rng.random() < 0.5
    if target_url:
        # map '+'->'-', '/'->'_' (standard to url)
        b64 = b64.translate(bytes.maketrans(b"+/", b"-_"))
    else:
        # map '-'->'+', '_'->'/' (url to standard)
        b64 = b64.translate(bytes.maketrans(b"-_", b"+/"))

    b64 = _maybe_strip_padding(rng, b64)
    b64 = _maybe_add_newlines(rng, b64)
    return b64


def _interesting_raws(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Curated cases to produce diverse base64 lengths and padding behaviors
    cases: List[bytes] = []
    cases.append(b"")
    cases.append(b"a")         # 1 byte -> 2 '=' padding when padded
    cases.append(b"ab")        # 2 bytes -> 1 '=' padding when padded
    cases.append(b"abc")       # 3 bytes -> no padding
    cases.append(b"abcd")
    cases.append(b"hello world")
    cases.append(b"\x00\x00\x00\xff\xff\xff\x01\x02\x03")
    cases.append(bytes(range(0, 256)))
    # random length blocks with bias around multiples of 3
    for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10]:
        n = rng.randint(1, 64)
        cases.append(_rand_bytes(rng, n*m % 97 + (m % 3)))
    # a few random sizes up to 512 bytes (stub trims to 512 anyway)
    for _ in range(5):
        cases.append(_rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 512)))
    return cases


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    raws = _interesting_raws(rng)
    raw = rng.choice(raws)
    b64 = _encode_payload(rng, raw)

    # Optionally wrap in a surrounding context that the stub will ignore after it re-encodes
    # Keep it pure base64 by default for highest validity.
    return b64[:4096]

import random
